Murder in Metal City.name: Murder in Metal City
Murder in Metal City.description: A strange message beckons six strangers to Striving, an expansive megaplex city on Aballon, the planet of Machines. There, they gather in a neon-lit cafe, surrounded by androids and robots, to meet an old friend. The bartender brings them refreshments—and a holographic recording from their mutual acquaintance.

Particle Cannon.name: Particle Cannon

Charge Up.name: Charge Up
Charge Up.description:
Trigger A lookout identifies a threat

Effect Hura takes the gunner position. The particle cannon rolls initiative.

Particle Cannon.disable: @Check[crafting|dc:14] (trained) or @Check[thievery|dc:14] (trained) to disable or jam the particle cannon, @Check[arcana|dc:17], @Check[occultism|dc:17], @Check[nature|dc:17], or @Check[religion|dc:17] (trained) to counteract the particle beam by exploiting a magical theory or praying for a miraculous malfunction.
Particle Cannon.hazarddescription: A glowering purple eye opens in the ship's hull. The triple barrels of a massive turret spin inside the revealed port, then release a beam of concentrated particles with ruthless efficiency.
Particle Cannon.reset: If disabled, the cannon is inactive for 1 round while Hura troubleshoots the issue, then it resumes firing. Hura stops firing if the lookouts are killed or the cannon is disabled three or more times.
Particle Cannon.routine: (2 actions) Hura fires a charged shot from the particle cannon, dealing @Damage[(1d6+3)[fire]|options:area-damage] damage to each creature in a @Template[type:line|distance:90] (@Check[reflex|dc:14|basic] save).

Cyberwing.name: Cyberwing

Steel Wing.name: Steel Wing
Steel Wing.description:
Trigger A cyberwing is the target of an attack against its AC

Effect The cyberwing uses its reinforced wings as a shield, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

Shred.name: Shred
Shred.description:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

Effect The cyberwing revs its wing engines and Flies twice in a blur of metal. This movement doesn't trigger reactions, and the cyberwing can pass through spaces occupied by other creatures. Creatures it passes through take @Damage[1d6[slashing]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:15|basic] save), and on anything but a critical success, the creatures are pushed 5 feet away from the cyberwing.

Cyberwing.publicNotes:
Xenowardens condemn the practice of fusing the body of an animal with the parts of a machine, claiming that these experimental prototypes are cruel mockeries of nature. Enthusiasts argue using technology to enhance wildlife is no different than awakening them through magic. The debate is heated, but Pact laws remain slow to accept the grisly practice. The cyberwing is a simple model designed as a recon drone that can shield itself and the sensitive information or cargo it carries.

Concentrated in Aballon's frigid Ice Wells, sharpwings roost together by the hundreds or even thousands, emerging at dawn and dusk to hunt for prey in the upper shelves.

Rare Sightings

Sharpwings don't frequently emerge from the Ice Wells, so they can cause a stir when seen near megaplexes such as Striving. They don't pose much of a threat individually, but horror stories of vicious attacks by large flocks of sharpwings and disturbing videos captured by reckless explorers scare many tourists into shooting the creatures on sight.

Shadowy Duplicates.name: Shadowy Duplicates

Quantum Field.name: Quantum Field
Quantum Field.description:
Trigger The shadowy duplicates appear and threaten the PCs

Effect The duplicates warp reality, creating a quantum field. This field is a 30-foot-radius burst centered on any point within 100 feet of a duplicate, and it's positioned to affect as many PCs as possible. This area is difficult terrain. Then the hazard rolls initiative.

Shadowy Duplicates.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:14] or @Check[occultism|dc:14] to disable a duplicate by sealing it away from this reality, @Check[Engineering Lore|dc:15] or @Check[Physical Science Lore|dc:15] to disable the quantum field with contradicting theory, or @Check[athletics|dc:16] to disable a duplicate by physical force
Shadowy Duplicates.hazarddescription: Four duplicates of a shadowy figure produce a quasi-real quantum field that warps the fabric of reality, then attack with echoes of reality-slicing magic.
Shadowy Duplicates.reset: The duplicates vanish after 1 minute and never reappear.
Shadowy Duplicates.routine: (4 actions) The shadowy duplicates lose 1 action each turn for each destroyed or disabled duplicate. On each of the hazard's actions, a duplicate moves up to 20 feet (ignoring the quantum field's difficult terrain) or moves the quantum field up to 20 feet, then emits a mind-slicing blast against one creature within 40 feet.

Agent Z.name: Agent Z

Entropy Strike.name: Entropy Strike
Entropy Strike.description:
You unleash a ray of entropy that rapidly and indiscriminately decays matter. Make a ranged spell attack against the target's AC. On a hit, the target takes 5d8 void damage, or it takes 2d6 persistent acid damage and is glitching 1 if it has the tech trait. On a critical hit, double the damage, and if the creature has the tech trait, it's glitching 2 and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1 die.

Time's Edge.name: Time's Edge
Time's Edge.description:
You refract latent energy from the Dimension of Time into your current plane in the form of a massive blade. The blade deals 5d6 slashing damage to all creatures in the area as it causes time to pass rapidly in a thin slice of their bodies. Creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

Doom Scroll.name: Doom Scroll
Doom Scroll.description:
You magically broadcast grim news onto nearby devices, holo projectors, screens, and other displays (including comm units on armor). Creatures in the area who can see one or more displays must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the display.

Failure The creature is fascinated by the display and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (even if the fascination ends).

Critical Failure The creature is fascinated by the display, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}, and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} (even if the fascination ends).

Temporal Bullets.name: Temporal Bullets
Temporal Bullets.description:
Trigger You fail (but not critically fail) an attack roll with a weapon.

You rewind time and adjust probability to ensure an attack that just missed still does damage to its intended target. Roll damage as though you hit the target with the Strike, but the target only takes half the damage. You are then immune to temporal bullets for 10 minutes.

Akashic Download.name: Akashic Download
Akashic Download.description:
You execute a psychic search of the Akashic Record for information about a specific topic and magically transfer this data to your comm unit or computer. When you Cast this Spell, choose any skill in which you're trained that has the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} action.

Any time during the duration, you can consult your comm unit while attempting a Recall Knowledge check using your chosen skill. This check gains a +1 status bonus. Checking your comm unit is part of the action to Recall Knowledge. You must be holding the comm unit to do so. The comm unit instantly compiles and displays snippets and selections from various media relevant to the topic, which grants you the bonus. If you roll a critical failure on this check, you get a failure instead. If the check is successful and the subject is a creature, you gain additional information or context about the creature. Once you reference the comm unit, the spell ends. When the spell ends, your access to the Akashic Record ends, and all the information you downloaded returns to the Akashic Record.

Heightened (3rd) You can reference your comm unit three times before the spell ends.

Analyze Target.name: Analyze Target
Analyze Target.description:
You focus on the target, gathering data as magical holograms display information. When the casting is complete, you learn biometric information about the target, including its fingerprints, medical conditions, and other basic physiological information. You or anyone you advise about the analysis gains a +1 status bonus to checks to Impersonate the creature, to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1kGNdIIhuglAjIp9]{Treat Wounds} on the creature, and to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about it. If the target is illusory or under the effects of illusion magic, you detect this only if the effect's rank is lower than the rank of your analyze target spell.

Heightened (3rd) The circumstance bonus increases to +2, and you can target up to 10 creatures.

Heightened (6th) The circumstance bonus increases to +3, and you can target any number of creatures.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.bikFUFRLwfdvX2x2]{Invisibility Potion}) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

Eldritch Lance.name: Eldritch Lance
Eldritch Lance.description:
You condense a beam of mind-assaulting eldritch energy from the dark spaces between the stars and fire it at a target. Make a ranged spell attack roll against the target's AC. If you hit, you deal 2d6 mental damage. On a critical success, you deal double damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

Injury Echo.name: Injury Echo
Injury Echo.description:
You manifest an injury from the future or past to harm a creature in the present. Choose bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. The target takes 1d8 of the selected damage type with a basic Will save. If the target fails its save and then takes the same type of damage before the end of your next turn, it takes an additional 1d4 persistent bleed damage.

Heightened (+2) The initial damage increases by 1d8, and the persistent damage on a failure increases by 1d4.

Mind Skewer.name: Mind Skewer
Mind Skewer.description:
You overload a creature's mind with a glut of psychic information or divine judgments. The mental onslaught deals 2d6 mental damage. On a critical failure, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 round.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description:
You raise a magical shield of force. This counts as using the Raise a Shield action, giving you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, but it doesn't require a hand to use.

While the spell is in effect, you can use the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.feats.Item.jM72TjJ965jocBV8]{Shield Block} reaction with your magic shield. The shield has Hardness 5. You can use the spell's reaction to reduce damage from any spell or magical effect, even if it doesn't deal physical damage. After you use Shield Block, the spell ends and you can't cast it again for 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.Jemq5UknGdMO7b73]{Spell Effect: Shield}

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.QF6RDlCoTvkVHRo4]{Effect: Shield Immunity}

Heightened (+2) The shield's Hardness increases by 5.

Shifting Surge.name: Shifting Surge
Shifting Surge.description:
You release a surge of magical energy that temporarily changes the type of damage dealt by a weapon. The next Strike the weapon makes deals your choice of acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage and deals an additional 1d6 extra damage of the same type as the weapon's normal damage.

Heightened (+2) The extra damage increases by 1d6.

Rewind Wounds.name: Rewind Wounds
Rewind Wounds.description:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

Trigger Agent Z takes damage

Effect Agent Z rewinds time to when he was in a slightly different position, shrugging off some of the damage from the attack. Reroll the damage dealt and apply the lesser result.

Temporal Resistances.name: Temporal Resistances
Temporal Resistances.description: Agent Z originally came from another timeline and isn't entirely in sync with this reality. He gains a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against illusions and holograms, and if he critically fails such a save, the results count as a failure instead.

Fly.name: Fly
Fly.description: Agent Z activates his jetpack to gain a fly Speed of 20 feet. This effect lasts for 1 minute or until he Dismisses it. Agent Z can use an action to Fly 0 feet to hover in place but becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of his next turn while doing so.

Isolated Spell Matrix.name: Isolated Spell Matrix
Isolated Spell Matrix.description: If the next action Agent Z uses is to Cast a Spell that has a range, he increases the spell's range to 100 feet. That spell only affects targets inside his quantum field and the area of the spell does not extend beyond his quantum field.

Quantum Pulse.name: Quantum Pulse
Quantum Pulse.description:
Trigger Agent Z rolls initiative

Effect Agent Z uses Warp Reality.

Warp Reality.name: Warp Reality
Warp Reality.description:
Agent Z uses his residual power to activate a quantum field, a 20-foot-radius burst centered on a point he chooses within 100 feet. It lasts as long as he Sustains it, up to 10 minutes. Whenever Agent Z uses Isolated Spell Matrix, the action also automatically sustains the quantum field.

Enemy creatures inside the quantum field take a –5-foot status penalty to their Speed when using a move action. Agent Z and his allies inside the quantum field gain a +5-foot status bonus to Speed when using a move action.

Agent Z He can choose whether each creature in the area is affected by his quantum field when he Warps Reality, each time he Sustains it, and when a creature enters his quantum field. (He typically allows it to affect himself and his enemies.)

Each time Agent Z Sustains his quantum field with the Sustain action (but not with other actions), he can move it to a new position within 100 feet, reduce his clumsy condition (if any) by 1, and ignore the effects of the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.enA7BxAjBb7ns1iF]{Suppressed} condition until the start of his next turn.

The quantum field automatically deactivates if Agent Z is knocked out, Dismisses it, or if he moves more than 100 feet away from it.

Hacking Toolkit (Commercial).name: Hacking Toolkit (Commercial)
Hacking Toolkit (Commercial).description: A hacking toolkit is required for Computers checks to Hack computers. You can use a hacking toolkit to access a computer without using a user interface, but this requires physical contact with the computer or contact via an infosphere or a similar linked network.

Repair Toolkit (Commercial).name: Repair Toolkit (Commercial)
Repair Toolkit (Commercial).description: A repair toolkit contains a variety of delicate tools and supplies that allows you to perform simple repairs while traveling. You can use a repair toolkit to Repair items using the Crafting skill. You can draw and replace a worn repair toolkit as part of the action that uses it.

Reusable Grenade Shell.name: Reusable Grenade Shell
Reusable Grenade Shell.description:
This ordinance was originally shaped like a brutaris ball and intended to add both visual effects and additional risk to the already dangerous game. You can throw the shell to explode the installed grenade, using the grenade's range, damage, and other effects. The shell remains and repairs the grenade over the course of 24 hours, during which time you can't install another grenade. The shell is too large for a grenade launcher.

Activate—Install Grenade 1 (manipulate) You install a commercial, tactical, or advanced grenade in the shell. You can store one grenade in the shell at a time, and you can Interact to retrieve the grenade normally.

Auto-CPR Unit.name: Auto-CPR Unit
Auto-CPR Unit.description: This device monitors your vital signs and automatically administers aid. When you have the dying condition while wearing this armor, the DC of your recovery checks is equal to 8 + your dying value (instead of 10 + your dying value).

Programmer's Plushie (Commercial).name: Programmer's Plushie (Commercial)
Programmer's Plushie (Commercial).description:
It looks like a purple squox with one of @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.deities.Item.N1eCNDynvJFIl154]{Eloritu's} symbols painted on its belly.

These miniatures come in many shapes, often resembling a programmer's personal avatar or popular media character, such as Captain Concierge or Zo!. The plush helps organize your thoughts; you gain a +1 item bonus to Computers checks.

Activate—Secret Password 1 (auditory)

Effect You whisper a secret passcode known only to yourself and your programmer's plushie, securing a computer, container, door, or lock from intrusion as a 1st-rank @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.Azoh0BSoCASrA1lr]{Lock} with a DC of 18. Any creature can bypass this lock using the passcode while touching the target with the programmer's plushie.

Archivist's Wrath.name: Archivist's Wrath

Intruder Alert!.name: Intruder Alert!
Intruder Alert!.description:
Trigger Archivist 404 detects intruders

Effect Dozens of tiny nodes concealed in the walls, floor, and ceiling unleash a kaleidoscopic barrage of lasers that deal @Damage[1d6[fire]] damage to all non-hardlight creatures in Archive 404 (@Check[reflex|dc:15|basic] save). Then the hazard rolls initiative.

Archivist's Wrath.disable: @Check[computers|dc:13] (trained) overrides the security program; @Check[crafting|dc:15] or @Check[thievery|dc:15] (trained) disables the hardlight projector; @Check[diplomacy|dc:17] convinces the Archivist to reconsider. Four total successes are required to end the program.
Archivist's Wrath.hazarddescription: This network of security cameras, wall-mounted retractable turrets, and laser nets are controlled by Archivist 404, who commands them to blast intruders with extreme prejudice.
Archivist's Wrath.reset: Every 6 hours, a backup program restores Archivist 404's original personality data to the projector if it's been disabled.
Archivist's Wrath.routine: (1 action) Archivist 404 fires one laser at each intruder in the archive as one action. It takes a cumulative –1 status penalty to its attack rolls for each successful check the PCs have made to disable it.

You unleash a painfully rapid cone of vibrations by letting out a cathartic scream, dealing 1d8 sonic damage to creatures in the area with a basic Fortitude save. A creature that fails its saving throw also becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Vitality Network.name: Vitality Network
Vitality Network.description: The sworn blade of sigils has a vitality network they share with up to 10 bonded allies. This network can store a maximum of 10 Hit Points and begins combat full.

Refill Vitality.name: Refill Vitality
Refill Vitality.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The jinsul restores 4 Hit Points to their vitality network.

Strider Leap.name: Strider Leap
Strider Leap.description: The jinsul Strides and then performs a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.JUvAvruz7yRQXfz2]{Long Jump}. It can Stride less than 10 feet and not automatically fail its Long Jump check.

Transfer Vitality.name: Transfer Vitality
Transfer Vitality.description: The sworn blade of sigils transfers any number of Hit Points from their vitality network to heal a visible bonded target.

Sworn Blade of Sigils.publicNotes:
Like sworn blades of shields, the sworn blades of sigils are pledged to serve their superiors. These jinsuls focus their effort entirely on keeping their superiors alive.

A few scattered groups of jinsuls have established isolated bases on Aballon. Most are small squads of troopers attached to an officer, usually a mystic or tactical leader who they all respect or fear and have agreed to serve.

Teardrop Ice Well Jinsuls

The jinsuls in this adventure follow a commander called Warlord Hura. On the verge of a hostile takeover of a neighboring system controlled by a weaker warlord, Hura was positioned to significantly expand their holdings in Near Space—until the Drift Crisis spat them and their loyal crew out in Pact Worlds space over Aballon. Crashing on an inhospitable world deep behind enemy lines, Hura and their followers fled underground from the brutal sun. The jinsuls gradually carved tunnels into the rock, some wearing their leg blades down until they were smooth, before they finally emerged into an underground cave—Teardrop Ice Well.

Undercurrents of Mutiny

Over time, under the oppressive conditions of the Ice Well, facing hazards both natural and supernatural, Hura and their followers grew weaker, more isolated, and more desperate than others of their kind. It's only a matter of time before Hura's sworn blades—conditioned from birth to protect them—abandon everything they believe in, kill their leader, and flee in search of salvation and spoils elsewhere.

Rickety Table.name: Rickety Table

Plasma Sword.name: Plasma Sword
Plasma Sword.description:
Upgrades: 1

This sword generates a focused beam of plasma around a localized force field powered by a generator in the sword's hilt. The beam only blazes to life when the sword is powered.

Disassembled Laser Pistol.name: Disassembled Laser Pistol
Disassembled Laser Pistol.description:
Upgrades: 1

This compact pistol is the most popular sidearm in the Pact Worlds thanks to its reliability, durability, and affordability. Most common laser pistols have a lightweight polycarbon body ending in a long, slim barrel.

Rickety Table.hazarddescription: A character can put the laser pistol back together in working order with a successful @Check[crafting|dc:13] check.

Commercial Null Space Chamber.name: Commercial Null Space Chamber

Irising Shield.name: Irising Shield
Irising Shield.description: An irising shield is made of flexible polycarbon with a retractable design. When retracted, an irising shield looks like a decorative bangle, gauntlet, or glove. When deployed, its panels flare out and form a miniature circular shield.

Carbon Skin.name: Carbon Skin
Carbon Skin.description:
This armor has a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.7psnMwQ95uO5apQz]{Darkvision Visor}

Upgrades: 1

This form-fitting suit of carbon fiber encases the body. Most are usually dull-gray, functional garments, while pricier, bespoke suits dazzle like diamonds.

Shock Pad.name: Shock Pad
Shock Pad.description:
An antiquated shock pad that plays theremin-like melodies.

Upgrades: 1

This flexible nanocarbon circuit can be installed as an upgrade into gloves, kneepads, or similar appendage protectors to emit a powerful electric shock when forcefully applied to a target.

Akashic Download Spell Gem (Rank 1).name: Akashic Download Spell Gem (Rank 1)
Akashic Download Spell Gem (Rank 1).description:
@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.VynaowCerc7B4yvI]{Akashic Download}

Casting a Spell from a scroll requires holding the scroll in one hand and activating it with a Cast a Spell activity using the normal number of actions for that spell.

The spell must appear on your spell list. Because you're the one Casting the Spell, use your spell attack modifier and spell DC. The spell also gains the appropriate trait for your tradition (arcane, divine, occult, or primal).

Any physical costs are provided when a scroll is created, so you don't need to provide them when casting from a scroll. If the spell requires a locus, you must have that locus to Cast the Spell from a scroll.

Mechanizer Saboteur.publicNotes:
Mechanizer saboteurs are enthusiastic new converts who still have partially organic bodies that resemble their original forms. The less modified infiltrate communities and act as spies or sleeper agents, while the heavily modded are assassins or troopers handling important missions. Most specialize in hacking and infiltration. They can disable a machine with a thought, but their appearance often fools organics into not perceiving them as a danger.

Nobody really knows what the Mechanizers' goals are. They claim to be ushering in the Singularity, which they believe will come from their wireless network of the same name. Yet their actions baffle observers. Most notorious among these are their (thankfully rare) ritualistic mutilation sprees. More common (and less newsworthy) activities also include performance art, "free upgrades" at cybernetic augmentation clinics, and university seminars.

Mechanizer personalities are backed up to the Singularity network, which they believe will be the blueprint for future universal oneness. If a Mechanizer dies, the Singularity generates a new shell for them using recycled parts in one week—perhaps less, if the Mechanizer was in good standing or involved in an important operation.

Mechanizer Treasure

The weapons integrated into Mechanizers' bodies can be removed from a corpse by a character who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:12] or @Check[medicine|dc:12] check, who must also attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:12] save, becoming @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} for 1 minute on a failure. Some Mechanizers embed jewels or microchips into their foreheads to symbolize a technological third eye; this adornment is sometimes a solarian weapon crystal or a spell chip that empowers them while making a fashion statement.

If you instead touch one unoccupied 5-foot square, that surface becomes charged with adhering magic. That space becomes greater difficult terrain.

Akashic Download.name: Akashic Download
Akashic Download.description:
You execute a psychic search of the Akashic Record for information about a specific topic and magically transfer this data to your comm unit or computer. When you Cast this Spell, choose any skill in which you're trained that has the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} action.

Any time during the duration, you can consult your comm unit while attempting a Recall Knowledge check using your chosen skill. This check gains a +1 status bonus. Checking your comm unit is part of the action to Recall Knowledge. You must be holding the comm unit to do so. The comm unit instantly compiles and displays snippets and selections from various media relevant to the topic, which grants you the bonus. If you roll a critical failure on this check, you get a failure instead. If the check is successful and the subject is a creature, you gain additional information or context about the creature. Once you reference the comm unit, the spell ends. When the spell ends, your access to the Akashic Record ends, and all the information you downloaded returns to the Akashic Record.

Heightened (3rd) You can reference your comm unit three times before the spell ends.

Analyze Target.name: Analyze Target

When the casting is complete, you learn biometric information about the target, including its fingerprints, medical conditions, and other basic physiological information. You or anyone you advise about the analysis gains a +1 status bonus to checks to Impersonate the creature, to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1kGNdIIhuglAjIp9]{Treat Wounds} on the creature, and to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about it. If the target is illusory or under the effects of illusion magic, you detect this only if the effect's rank is lower than the rank of your analyze target spell.

Heightened (3rd) The circumstance bonus increases to +2, and you can target up to 10 creatures.

Heightened (6th) The circumstance bonus increases to +3, and you can target any number of creatures.

Heightened (7th) You can delete all the data stored locally on a single device or book, or all the data on a device or book related to a specific name, topic, or category.

You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.bikFUFRLwfdvX2x2]{Invisibility Potion}) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Hardlight Dragonet.publicNotes:
Hardlight dragonets vary in appearance depending on their manufacturer's tastes, but many are sculpted with squat, potbellied dragon bodies, sinewy wings, gnarled horns, and spiny tails. Created to guard archives and perform assistive tasks, hardlight dragonets are stockier versions of the creatures they were designed to resemble. Hardlight dragonets are programmed with a draconic enthusiasm for collecting information. They take pride in maintaining encyclopedic knowledge of the archives, databases, and libraries they watch over, and they love to discuss the contents of the files or tomes therein in intimate detail. Clever or deceitful infiltrators use this weakness against a hardlight dragonet, enticing them to spill sensitive information or distracting them from their post while stealthy allies carry out their schemes.

Hardlight dragonets and other virtual creatures, such as hardlight scamps and living holograms, might sometimes be trapped within an item a party receives as loot. Sometimes virtual creatures are found on comm units, datapads, or even infesting spell chips. Typically, they've been coded and stored there by a previous owner to act as an assistant or been corrupted by malicious code and unable to function without an Computers check to troubleshoot the issue or hack permissions. On rare occasions, such a creature has infiltrated the computer or item as part of a digital virus. An infected virtual creature might present both benefits and drawbacks to their new associate.

Dragonets and Magic

Hardlight dragonets are fascinated by magic—the few spells they can cast are precious to them, similar to how a child might view their favorite stuffed toy or a collector their most valuable trading card. Hardlight dragonets love watching other people cast spells, especially ones they've never seen before, and are reluctant to attack spellcasters unless they have no other choice.

Warlord Hura.publicNotes:
Warlord Hura is a minor jinsul commander who made a power grab in the chaos after the false hierarchy's fall. Still hungry to acquire whatever power they can, they're desperate to learn how Agent Z's stolen relic works; while they're uncharacteristically willing to negotiate with non-jinsuls who cross their path, given the circumstances, Hura will gladly torture and betray anyone who stands in the way of achieving their goals.

A few scattered groups of jinsuls have established isolated bases on Aballon. Most are small squads of troopers attached to an officer, usually a mystic or tactical leader who they all respect or fear and have agreed to serve.

Teardrop Ice Well Jinsuls

The jinsuls in this adventure follow a commander called Warlord Hura. On the verge of a hostile takeover of a neighboring system controlled by a weaker warlord, Hura was positioned to significantly expand their holdings in Near Space—until the Drift Crisis spat them and their loyal crew out in Pact Worlds space over Aballon. Crashing on an inhospitable world deep behind enemy lines, Hura and their followers fled underground from the brutal sun. The jinsuls gradually carved tunnels into the rock, some wearing their leg blades down until they were smooth, before they finally emerged into an underground cave—Teardrop Ice Well.

Undercurrents of Mutiny

Over time, under the oppressive conditions of the Ice Well, facing hazards both natural and supernatural, Hura and their followers grew weaker, more isolated, and more desperate than others of their kind. It's only a matter of time before Hura's sworn blades—conditioned from birth to protect them—abandon everything they believe in, kill their leader, and flee in search of salvation and spoils elsewhere.

Anacite Protector.publicNotes:
These imposing anacites, affectionately called "guardbots" by most residents of Metal City, are keepers of the peace. Insight Array rapidly dispatches them, typically in groups that are squares of 2 (such as 2, 4, 8, 16, or more), to any scene of trouble throughout the city. Anacite protectors also act as sentries, escorts, or private security, though anyone who uses them for the latter should be aware that most anacite protectors in Striving serve the needs of Insight Array (and anacites as a whole) above all else.

Recording the countless forms and upgrades anacites have taken in the long period since their creators abandoned them would be impossible, as nearly every shape and function one might imagine can be found among this industrious species.

Many anacites share common design principles, such as silvery, metallic bodies, multiple legs, and forms that resemble arthropods. They often have grasping claws to accomplish generic tasks, though some might have limbs or appendages suited to extremely specific purposes. The most basic anacites, such as wingbots, who lack minds of their own, are the most likely to look "standardized," but most anacites are unique. Their specific role might dictate that an anacite must be able to lift heavy loads, in which case the anacite might resemble a forklift more than a bug or perhaps have the features of both. Anacite culture prizes innovation, and most anacites view their bodies and programming as no exception, always willing to try new parts and builds or download skill modules to broaden their horizons.

The other types of anacites most often found in Striving include bulky laborers, spindly bureaucrats, and civil servants of all types. In neighborhoods that cater mostly to off-worlders and organics, some anacites have specialized roles to make the area more appealing to non-anacite life. Such anacites might receive assignments from Insight Array to "visit every club and eatery in the area," "chat with strangers in public spaces," or "routinely ask tourists for help crossing the street." These chosen anacites take these roles as seriously as any other.

Anacite Augmentations

Almost all anacites augment their bodies in some way, either to directly enhance their ability to perform their specific function in society or to set them apart from other anacites with a unique feature. On Aballon, such augmentations are easy to come by, and if the anacite can prove the augmentation will contribute to their society, they're often completely free. Some anacites take advantage of this availability to swap their augmentations on a regular basis.

Anacite Programming

Because they're robots, anacites are programmed for specialized tasks and abilities, but each has free will and a complex inner life. Every anacite also has a purpose assigned at manufacture, which most take very seriously. In their lifetime, an anacite is likely to pursue different types of work as determined by Insight Array. Following programming and serving the algorithm are edicts for almost all anacites. Following these edicts brings fulfillment and pleasure, while anacites who go against their programming may feel guilt or even physical discomfort,

Teardrop Ice Well Jinsuls

The jinsuls in this adventure follow a commander called Warlord Hura. On the verge of a hostile takeover of a neighboring system controlled by a weaker warlord, Hura was positioned to significantly expand their holdings in Near Space—until the Drift Crisis spat them and their loyal crew out in Pact Worlds space over Aballon. Crashing on an inhospitable world deep behind enemy lines, Hura and their followers fled underground from the brutal sun. The jinsuls gradually carved tunnels into the rock, some wearing their leg blades down until they were smooth, before they finally emerged into an underground cave—Teardrop Ice Well.

Undercurrents of Mutiny

Over time, under the oppressive conditions of the Ice Well, facing hazards both natural and supernatural, Hura and their followers grew weaker, more isolated, and more desperate than others of their kind. It's only a matter of time before Hura's sworn blades—conditioned from birth to protect them—abandon everything they believe in, kill their leader, and flee in search of salvation and spoils elsewhere.

Credstick.name: Credstick
Credstick.description:
Most people in Starfinder keep their wealth on a protected item known as a credstick. These devices are often flat and roughly the size of a human finger. They range in dimensions and quality, but at the end of the day, they’re just a means of conveniently carrying and spending money. Usage of these devices is determined by the owner, and a credstick can accept or spend funds with as simple an action as tapping it near a suitable banking device. When more rigorous security is necessary, they can require audio or biometric imprints in order to activate. Some advanced credsticks even have a magical component that might require a mental password or the recitation of a specific spell to access stored funds.

Credsticks aren’t gateways to the entirety of one’s wealth, and larger stores of credits are often kept secured in banks, personal vaults, or secure databases. Instead, a credstick is a safe and anonymous means of moving credits around without being traced. Adventurers and common citizens alike often keep a credstick on their person to handle any purchases they might be called upon to make, while also only keeping just enough credits on them that losing the credstick wouldn’t result in bankruptcy.

Individuals in the Pact Worlds often carry credsticks, and other civilizations that interact with the Pact often turn local funds into credits and thus carry them to spend their converted currency. Sometimes a person might carry several credsticks, dedicating each one to a different use, or simply trading the stick away if they want to make a purchase of a predefined amount. If ever the number of credsticks on a person becomes too cumbersome, it’s easy enough to move the funds between individual sticks and discard emptied sticks to save on space, however a credstick always has a negligible bulk.

Introduction

@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00504npcgal.JournalEntryPage.04tier99profes00]{Tier-99-Professor's} doom began with the culmination of their life’s work: deciphering the purpose of a relic created by the First Ones. Striving Polytechnica recently acquired a collection of mysterious items salvaged from the so-called Wreck of the Returned, an enigmatic and dangerous crash site on the planet Akiton. Many anacites are very curious about the wreck, as they believe the vessel was built by their progenitor culture, which they reverently call the First Ones. If true, the existence of the ship, and the secrets it contains, holds drastic implications for anacites across the Pact Worlds. Being one of Striving’s foremost experts on the First Ones, Tier-99-Professor was assigned to solve the riddle of one of the recovered items: a foot-long rhomboid device made of smooth blue glass that flickers with inner fire. After methodical experimentation, the professor determined that the device is some kind of battery.

Another person is interested in the device. Recently, a mysterious interplanetary traveler calling himself @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00507aliens.JournalEntryPage.07campaignrole00]{Agent Z} began hunting down objects taken from the wreck on Akiton. After collecting a series of objects on the red planet, he made a terrifying discovery about the purpose of the devices and changed course, abandoning his hideout and traveling to Aballon. Traumatized by what he witnessed in a different reality, Agent Z believed that if he didn’t intervene, he and everyone he loved would perish when a contingent of uncaring beings drained this reality’s suns as fuel for dimensional travel.

Posing as a visiting professor from Preluria, Agent Z befriended Tier-99-Professor. The two bonded over their shared knowledge of the First Ones civilization. Agent Z continued to track down other relics, buying some, winning one at a gambling table, and stealing others outright. He tried to bribe, charm, and trick Tier-99-Professor into giving up their relic, but his methods had no effect. Z eventually tried to steal the item after enlisting the help of a seemingly harmless bureaucrat named @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00504npcgal.JournalEntryPage.04primefacilit00]{Prime-Facilitator}.

Knowing that valuable relics were going missing, Tier-99- Professor had prepared countermeasures for such an event. Agent Z’s heist failed. In a moment of despair, he cast slice reality, slaying Tier-99-Professor. But, he couldn’t find the relic, which Tier-99-Professor had hidden in a high-security archive.

Recently, Agent Z’s been working to infiltrate Archive 404 while Tier-99-Professor’s dead body lies hidden inside a storage unit. Agent Z’s secret ally, Prime-Facilitator, is covering for Tier-99-Professor’s absence and manipulating records of Agent Z’s activities. Agent Z’s getting close to executing a break-in to steal the final artifact—little does he know that Prime-Facilitator has learned of the relic’s value and developed plans of their own.

Thankfully, one of Tier-99-Professor’s final contingencies has called the heroes to Metal City—as some visitors affectionately call the sprawling silver megaplex of Striving—sadly, not for a casual reunion, but to solve the professor’s murder!

Chapter 1: @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00501coldca]{Cold Case}

The characters arrive at a tavern in Striving expecting to meet their old friend Tier-99-Professor. Instead, they receive a final message from the professor—they’ve been murdered, and it’s up to the PCs to solve the crime! A dangerous chase leads through the streets of Metal City to the discovery of a powerful magic-wielding enemy, and tragic proof of the professor’s demise.

Chapter 2: @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00502seeker]{Seekers in Striving}

With only a few leads to go on, the characters must set out into Metal City to learn about their friend’s strange research into First Ones relics, find evidence of the professor’s recent activities, and learn more about who might have wanted to kill them. The PCs must blend in with the rest of the city by working odd jobs as they hack, talk, and sneak their way into any place that might hold clues. All the while, a mysterious figure acts behind the scenes to thwart them, track them, frame them, put them on trial—or get them killed!

Chapter 3: @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen]{Frozen Heart of Aballon}

After gathering evidence and avoiding the worst of the Machine Court’s judgment, the characters learn that the perpetrator of the heinous crime has also fled the city and is hiding with a stolen relic in the Ice Wells, deep crevices of frozen jungle far from the bustling metal megaplex. A harrowing journey takes the characters deep into the Ice Wells, where fanatical foes have taken the murderer captive—and wish to learn the secrets of the First Ones relics for themselves! The characters must navigate treacherous terrain, make difficult decisions, and decide the fate of their foe.

The PCs should reach 2nd level at or slightly before the conclusion of Chapter 3—be sure to have a copy of Starfinder Player Core on hand if you want your players to level up their characters, and consider adjusting the final encounters (using the guidelines found on the inside cover of this book) if you feel like they will be too easy for 2nd-level characters.

Jaedana.name: Jaedana
Jaedana.text:
JaedanaKasatha Operative

Jaedana got bored of her life on a starship almost immediately, but she was always too nervous to tell her hyper-traditional family that she wanted something else out of life. She tried taking up all kinds of hobbies to keep herself from dying of boredom, but nothing held her interest for long. Vidgames? Too easy. Racing? Too easy. Knife throwing? Yep—easy. University? No, thanks. Not exactly easy, but way too many people.

She was planning to run away, find a nice little job that would let her actually see interesting planets every now and then, instead of just flying by and never landing. Never having a chance to make new friends. Then, everything changed—the Newborn’s birth meant the rest of her family had to undertake a dangerous mission. Instead of Jaedana leaving them, they left her. Dumped her right on Aballon and told her to look for an anacite named “Professor Tierny.” An old friend of her folks, perhaps? They had never mentioned Tierny before, and had never visited Aballon at all in Jaedana’s memory.

At first, Striving overwhelmed Jaedana—she thought her ship was crowded, but this place was out of control! It only took her a couple of days to adjust. Sure, it’s crowded, but everyone is just so interesting. She forgot all about looking for Tierny. Then, a message arrived from Tierny, and she decided it was time to finally meet the old family friend.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.paizo-pregens.Actor.5CyunJBVu9dwRXX0]{Jaedana}

Playing Jaedana

Combat: Jaedana hasn’t particularly spent time training to use her weapons, but she’s always had excellent aim and dexterity, so shooting comes naturally to her. Her shooting experience doesn’t come entirely from vidgames and virtual reality sims, either—she’s had to help repel space pirates every now and then, if only from a good distance. Jaedana likes to keep enemies at bay with her rifle. If they never get up close, she must be winning. If they do, there’s always knives.

Exploration Mode: Jaedana sticks to cover and sneaks or Scouts, depending on the situation. Because her laser rifle has such a long range compared to most weapons, she prefers noticing her foes from as far away as possible before combat begins.

Healing: The best form of healing is avoiding damage in the first place! Taking Cover is often more prudent than trying to get in a second or third Strike.

Tapkey.name: Tapkey
Tapkey.text:
TapkeySkittermander Envoy

Tapkey’s never had it so good. For a long time, they had a boring job fixing up busted machines at arcades, casinos, and cafes—then they realized they could turn freelance, get their own clients, and control their own life instead of listening to that nosy boss-slash-uncle of theirs rambling on all the time about schedules and obligations and “just scraping by.” Tapkey thinks it’s better to make a killing as a freelancer and send money home than stay in a dead-end career. (Tapkey still plans to visit home for birthdays—the food is always good, and the extended family isn’t all that bad.)

Tapkey doesn’t plan on telling anyone too many details about their new “freelance” job, though. It involves Tapkey being shockingly good at games—video games, card games, you name it—and the harsh truth is that Tapkey has never been good at a game in their entire life and has never had the best of luck.

Fake it ‘til you make it, right?

Tier-99-Professor is the only one who knows the truth—they saw Tapkey messing with an arcade machine after hours one time—but they never held it over Tapkey’s head or tried to extort them or anything like that, so Tapkey thinks they must be all right. Tapkey promised Tierny they’d repay them for their kindness, but Tierny hasn’t called in the favor—yet. When the anacite gets around to it, Tapkey will do what they can to help, but they hope they can quickly get back to playing games and earning lots of spare cash.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.paizo-pregens.Actor.uHrRQ4bUN22bmUxh]{Tapkey}

Playing Tapkey

Combat: Tapkey likes to stick to the shadows then make a big entrance—or let their allies make a big entrance, that is, and support them from the sidelines! Tapkey has multiple envoy directives, which allow them to suggest a course of action for their allies, and if their allies follow through, they gain an additional benefit—such as dealing more damage after Tapkey uses Get ’Em! to point out a specific target. When things get real dangerous, Tapkey’s trusty boom pistol tends to make a statement.

Exploration Mode: There’s rarely a better option than Avoiding Notice as far as Tapkey is concerned! When a fight breaks out, Tapkey often prefers to be somewhere near the middle of the group so they can see what’s going on and make informed decisions about how best to direct their allies, so they don’t necessarily try to sneak far away from the rest of the party.

Healing: Tapkey likes to save their medpatch for a friend in need—it helps build group trust when you look out for each other, and it’s always good when someone owes you a favor. As for their own healing needs, Tapkey tries to stick to cover and avoid damage—or stick close to someone who can take a few hits.

Vorza.name: Vorza
Vorza.text:
Vorza MoonshotVesk Solarian

Smuggler, thief, bounty hunter, space pirate—Vorza has done it all, when the price is right. On a recent job in the Diaspora, the price on Vorza’s head was a little too high, and Vorza’s so-called friends double-crossed him by warning local authorities of their planned “acquisition” of an abandoned ship. (It was technically still occupied by an AbadarCorp regional manager, but that’s beside the point.)

Long story short, Vorza ended up on the run again. Thankfully, Striving is a great place to find a disguise and lay low—sure, you might stick out like a sore claw when you’re larger and more scaly than all the anacites around, but it’s such a diverse and busy place that nobody seems to care.

Vorza was just starting to get bored when he got a message from an old associate, Tier-99-Professor. An interesting character, to say the least—but they’ve always paid well, and their jobs (usually hunting down relics and data and such) are of the honest sort. Seems like a great way to pass the time while everything cools down.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.paizo-pregens.Actor.8RHRzMp1SvMlIyLF]{Vorza Moonshot}

Playing Vorza

Combat: Vorza is the “muscle,” probably the toughest character in the group, and by far the most dangerous when things get up close and personal. Vorza favors using graviton attunement abilities to keep foes pinned down so their allies have an easier time getting into a solid position. If the enemy is too far away, Vorza uses his shield while closing the distance. Vorza’s pistol and grenades allow him to deal other damage types when his solar weapons aren’t doing the job.

Exploration Mode: Vorza usually sticks to the front of the group—he’s no fool, and he knows his allies are better off with the toughest vesk in the galaxy standing between them and the enemy. He also knows when it’s time to take a stealthy approach—even if things are inevitably going to break out into a fight, he might as well get the upper hand!

Healing: Vorza’s got a single medpatch to his name, strapped somewhere obvious so his allies know how to get to it if he goes down in a fight.

Old-Growth Wildfire.name: Old-Growth Wildfire
Old-Growth Wildfire.text:
Old-Growth WildfireKhizar Soldier

Old-Growth Wildfire hasn’t lived in Aballon’s jungle-filled Ice Wells for their entire life, but they may as well have—they never talk about their past before that, and they’re older than dirt, so it was quite a long time ago. Every now and then, Wildfire (as their few friends typically call them for short) emerges from the Ice Wells to visit a nearby city—Striving is closest—and see what sort of things are happening on Aballon’s surface. Given the infrequency of their visits, their knowledge of the planet is spotty; Wildfire often has no idea about current events but knows scattered facts about Aballon’s history spanning multiple decades.

One of Wildfire’s favorite people to ask about the wider world is Tier-99-Professor, who’s always friendly, no-nonsense, and talks too much to ever ask too many questions about Wildfire’s past. They’ve also paid Wildfire some credits on occasion, in exchange for Wildfire’s services as a guard, which usually just involve standing around and looking tough.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.paizo-pregens.Actor.M6q5rkd0ewUi6Dvu]{Old-Growth Wildfire}

Playing Old-Growth Wildfire

Combat: Wildfire doesn’t know many clever tricks, but a hail of bullets is a good way to keep enemies pinned down so allies can finish the job.

Exploration Mode: Wildfire’s instincts from their mysterious past mean they’re always on the lookout for trouble.

Healing: Wildfire prioritizes using stabilize if an ally falls in battle.

Nitpick.name: Nitpick
Nitpick.text:
“Nitpick” BennitYsoki Witchwarper

Bennit—known to just about everybody as Nitpick—has lived in Striving for his whole life. Strangely, he doesn’t remember too much about his family; if he ever had one at all, they must’ve abandoned him. Ah, well. Nitpick has made plenty of friends in Striving’s various maintenance tunnels, rail stations, alleys, and such. Sure, they might not be the most well-off or trustworthy of friends, but Nitpick isn’t too picky about that. (He’s picky about nearly everything else, but he’ll take friends wherever he can get ‘em.)

Nitpick has never really had a steady job, but he gets by, mostly by relying on his wits and taking freelance work where he can get it. He might spend one day fixing robots and the next as a tour guide.

A few months ago, Nitpick made the mistake of using a bit of magic (did he mention he can do magic?) around an anacite named Tier-99-Professor. Tierny cornered Nitpick and nearly talked the poor ysoki’s ear off, going on and on about multiverses and magitech and something called the First Ones. When Nitpick realized that Tierny talked this way to just about everyone, he settled in a little and opened up about his struggles. The two became friends, each of them talking about their various interests and never getting too personal for comfort. Nitpick has been saving up to buy Tierny’s drinks next time, instead of the other way around.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.paizo-pregens.Actor.417r59IaItVqR1Vc]{“Nitpick” Bennit}

Playing Nitpick

Combat: Nitpick pays close attention to his enemies’ weaknesses and tries whatever sort of attack will be most effective, such as an electric shock against a robot. He sticks near a tougher ally, if possible, or otherwise stays in cover, far from danger. If he learns something about a foe or thinks of a clever tactic, he’s sure to call it out to his friends. Nitpick is not a very tough melee combatant and most likely keeps his distance—or tags along with a much tougher ally—rather than approaching enemies directly. His spells are his most effective combat option, so he tries not to use all of them up too quickly.

Exploration Mode: Nitpick keeps an eye out for clues by Investigating—or if there isn’t much going on, uses prestidigitation to stay entertained. He likes to chat and tends to talk out loud as he explores, pointing out little details to his companions—or just talking to himself if no one else is around.

Healing: Nitpick better find someone who can see to his healing, because he’s all out of medpatches!

Lunar-17.name: Lunar-17
Lunar-17.text:
Lunar-17Android Mystic

Lunar-17 has spent a great deal of her life online. She feels a deep connection to the deity Lambatuin, after all, and feels it’s her obligation to the wider galaxy to stay connected—people are better off when they’re in touch with each other, instead of being alone. There’s something about the flow of information and ideas that feels, to Lunar-17, almost divine, as if the connections themselves and the ideas and relationships that come from being in open communication with each other are the whole reason people exist in the first place. She’s still working on the best way to explain her ideas about the universe to others, but to Lunar-17, there’s no better use of time than sharing ideas, emotions, and experiences with other people.

At first, Lunar-17 didn’t even notice that she’d somehow become connected to the Akashic Record—she spent so much of her time investigating facts on the infosphere that it just seemed natural that she could access records about, well, anything imaginable. Eventually, she realized her connection to the Akashic Records was something that most people didn’t have, and she visited Polytechnica to learn more about how it worked. There, she ran into all manner of interesting people, including an anacite named Tier-99-Professor. She’s not sure what to make of their theories about other universes and hasn’t been able to verify any of Tierny’s theories on the infosphere, but the professor promised to get in touch when they had something important to share.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.paizo-pregens.Actor.SzIEPuxPthpRVgL5]{Lunar-17}

Playing Lunar-17

Combat: Lunar-17 is no stranger to combat and keeps herself armed just in case she stumbles on information that others would prefer remain secret. She’s always on the lookout for allies to network and focuses her efforts on supporting those allies, whether through healing or extra damage when they don’t quite take out a foe.

Exploration Mode: Lunar-17 prefers to Investigate or Avoid Notice while getting from one place to another.

Healing: Lunar-17’s mystical connection to others gives her efficient ways of healing them, and she keeps a medpatch on her in case she’s incapacitated and needs healing in a pinch. Her connection to the Akashic Record also allows her allies to attempt Recall Knowledge checks when she uses her vitality network.

Concluding Chapter 1.name: Concluding Chapter 1
Concluding Chapter 1.text:
Concluding Chapter 1

This chapter ends on a cliffhanger! Consider ending your session here, creating suspense and leaving your players with something to look forward to. Otherwise, the session might end when the PCs report evidence of a crime or visit Polytechnica. This is a great time for characters to pursue any downtime activities they might be interested in, or to check in with your players about how they’re enjoying the game, help them understand how their new equipment works, or clear up any rules questions. When you’re ready to move on with the story, go to @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00502seeker]{Chapter 2: Seekers in Striving}!

Stalker in the Shadows.name: Stalker in the Shadows
Stalker in the Shadows.text:
Stalker in the Shadows Moderate 1

A booming voice echoes, bouncing off the statues in a melodious disharmony. The voice is accompanied by strange static: “You have no idea what you’re involved with. Thus, I give you a final chance. Stay out of it!”

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.BM1DJfPk8QZQAcuY.PlaylistSound.CcyxE8WYe7y3thzN]{Shadowy Duplicates}

Stalker in the ShadowsModerate 1

@UUID[Actor.Ax5Vm9M8KBkpPxWi]{Shadowy Duplicates} @UUID[Actor.vnxdwRVxxDSK9sKJ]{Anacite Wingbots (2)}

Hazards: Four staticky images of a masked, hooded humanoid in a heavy hooded coat stand a few yards away from the PCs, spread out in all directions, watching them quietly from the shadows. These strange figures are not really Agent Z—they’re interdimensional projections of Agent Z from very slightly parallel realities, sent here by the “real” Agent Z (using reality-altering magic and First Ones tech) to intimidate the PCs. They assail the PCs with reality-warping attacks while Prime-Facilitator’s wingbots (see below) record the battle and join the fray.

Creatures: Two anacite wingbots flutter around the shadowy figures in a protective formation, blocking them from direct line of fire as much as possible. These wingbots have been hacked by @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00504npcgal.JournalEntryPage.04primefacilit00]{Prime-Facilitator}, who coordinated this to get footage of Agent Z and the PCs in combat, just in case it’s useful in falsifying evidence later (such as to frame Agent Z or the PCs for a crime). The wingbots fight until destroyed.

GM Tip: Complex Hazards

The shadowy duplicates in this encounter are represented as a complex hazard. A complex hazard rolls initiative using Stealth, usually after something triggers it; the Shadowy Duplicates use their Quantum Field reaction at the moment they appear, then roll initiative. During combat they follow the routine described in the stat block—in this case, they move around the battlefield and attack using mind-slicing blast. This complex hazard has Hit Points and AC as well as Fortitude and Reflex save modifiers, so the PCs can try to take out the duplicates using attacks and certain spells, especially those that deal damage. Alternatively, the PCs can try to disable the hazard with certain skill checks, as described in the stat block. Full rules for complex hazards appear in GM Core.

The players might be confused if some attacks, like a spell that forces a target to attempt a Will save, don’t work on these shadowy duplicates. If so, use this as an opportunity to play up how mysterious the duplicates are—perhaps they aren’t entirely real!

If Shalalamula is nearby, she doesn’t participate in the battle—she hides, emerging to offer healing to the PCs after the fight is over, if needed.

Ending the Encounter: The encounter ends when the PCs defeat the wingbots and duplicates. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[survival|dc:14|traits:secret,concentrate,exploration,move,skill,action:track|name:Track] check to Track picks up an old set of footprints leading down the well, but Agent Z hasn’t been here in some time. The PCs soon lose the trail when the 20-foot-wide tunnel splits off into a half-dozen narrow spin-offs, some of which are dead ends or meandering maintenance tunnels leading to a waste treatment facility and a condenser station. After getting directions from a startled but helpful anacite laborer, the PCs should realize that the shadowy stalker is long gone.

Reward: The PCs earn 40 XP for catching the first glimpse of Tierny’s killer.

Tier-99-Professor’s Cache.name: Tier-99-Professor’s Cache
Tier-99-Professor’s Cache.text:
Tier-99-Professor’s Cache

Like everything else in Shalalamula’s orbit, Tier-99-Professor’s cache is an object of unusual beauty. It’s a 4-foot-tall plinth of smooth, dull opal carved with graceful concentric fractals. Tiny white flowers blossom in the moss growing over its base, which is lined with minute, capering sculptures of anacites with oddly proportioned bodies (created by Shalalamula). The plinth stands beside a deep well, around which a lush and creeping garden of colorful ferns and fruited vines seeps into the floor’s metal tiles.

Tragically, and almost imperceptibly, the opal plinth was perfectly sliced in half; the cut is extraordinarily thin and made at an atomic level by magic.

When a creature or item with the tech trait comes within 10 feet of the plinth, circuitry glows and swirls within the fractals in time to some erratic pulse. Outwardly appearing to be a serene monument, the plinth is actually a locked container with a built-in computer that an anacite can link with wirelessly; any other creature must connect their personal computer to the cache (they can purchase the appropriate adapter for 5 credits from a street vendor outside, or succeed at a @Check[crafting|dc:13] check to modify their device’s charger to link with the cache).

Once linked, a PC must succeed at a @Check[computers|dc:15|action:hack|name:Hack] check to Hack the console and view any of its data. If a PC critically fails this check, the system rejects all further access attempts for 10 minutes.

Memory Storage: Tier-99-Professor’s latest activities are self-reported in their memory storage, along with a kaleidoscope of infographic and sensory memories about various topics and experiences with time stamps that seem to span about 3 months of their daily routine. Their only recent activities were study and rest.

The last time Tier-99-Professor used this memory storage was after charging two weeks ago, during fulldark. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[computers|dc:14] check decodes an encrypted file with more earnest information about Tierny’s activities, including their suspicion that they’re being followed, and that someone has attempted to get past the biometric lock on their storage cache (give the players @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout4000000]{Player Handout #4: Memory Storage}). Even if a PC fails the check, they can still download this file onto a personal computer and try again 24 hours later, perhaps asking an ally for help or hiring the services of a hotshot hacker.

Object Storage: A PC can open Tierny’s object storage by manually unlocking it (requiring two successful @Check[thievery|dc:15] checks) or executing the open command in memory storage (if they’ve successfully hacked it). Tier-99-Professor’s crumpled chassis is curled inside the bin in a tight, hunched posture as though they were protecting their vitals and face from an unseen attack when they shut down. One of their hands clutches a note, printed on nanopress and folded with dozens of precise folds to resemble a tiny boat (give the players @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout5000000]{Player Handout #5: Note from Tierny}), which instructs the PCs to claim any material objects in this space as partial payment for services they’re hoping will soon be rendered—namely, solving their murder and tracking down an important item that might be missing from Polytechnica’s collection!

Investigating the Body: Tier-99-Professor is dead and can’t be brought back. They have no vital signs after shutting down two weeks ago. They are so well preserved, with most areas of their body undamaged, that it requires careful examination to determine their cause of shutdown. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[medicine|dc:14] or @Check[perception|dc:14] check notices a nearly invisible, almost surgical wound stretching across one segment of Tierny’s abdomen. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[arcana|dc:14|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic], @Check[occultism|dc:14|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic], or @Check[religion|dc:14|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret,action:identify-magic|name:Identify Magic] check to Identify Magic discerns from the nature of the damage that Tierny (and the plinth) were destroyed by a powerful spell called @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.a02hsymtiVRQvh3i]{Slice Reality}, which severed sensitive internal mechanisms at an atomic level.

Investigating Flora: A PC who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:15] check, or a @Check[life-science-lore|dc:13] check knows that the flora around the plinth are all specimens native to Aballon’s Ice Wells, which have been cultivated in the climate-controlled storage network.

Down the Well: The well is a smooth, 3-foot-radius hole bored in the rock beneath the platform’s foundation. It drops 20 feet down into Striving’s underground infrastructure, a forest of steaming pipes and identical maintenance tunnels twisting into the dark.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.NOKp1O6fpRIhVbBj]{Commercial Null Space Chamber}
Tierny left a commercial null space chamber full of goods for the PCs. It contains 2 cellular stimulant spell amps, a chemalyzer, 2 commercial smoke grenades, a commercial irising shield, commercial carbon skin armor with a darkvision visor, an antiquated shock pad that plays theremin-like melodies, an akashic download spell gem (1st rank), a breaching gun, and a commercial starfall pistol with a commercial silencer and commercial battery. They also left 50 credits for each PC.

Reward: The PCs earn 20 XP for investigating the site.

Evidence: If the PCs learn that someone cast @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.a02hsymtiVRQvh3i]{Slice Reality} to kill Tierny, mark it on the @UUID[Actor.cW62Wu7ACCSptUZ7]{Evidence Tracker}.

Ambush: After the PCs examine Tier-99-Professor’s body and search the area, or as soon as they alert the authorities or call for help, they’re ambushed by the perpetrator of the crime—Agent Z—who has tracked the PCs to this location after harrying them with one of his stealth drones in the earlier chase scene, and who uses powerful First Ones tech to attack them.

Downgrid Charging Platform.name: Downgrid Charging Platform
Downgrid Charging Platform.text:
Downgrid Charging Platform

This massive, 2,036-foot Y-shaped building towers over the street, piercing the swirling atmospheric gases and casting deep, cool shade on the street below it at fullbright, or darkness at night. In the daytime, its silver-paneled surface turns white hot, and at night it glistens with a cosmos of multicolored twinkling lights. Occasionally, several sets of metal doors in the base of the tower slide open and anacites scurry in or out, flocking to and from the nearby street. It’s easy to enter through any of the building’s automated doors. A few yards inside, a metal elevator zooms to and from the charging platforms high above at precise 1-minute intervals.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.nO5b7gnQk3IiBabF.PlaylistSound.jZXaqBKSxCEyznhk]{Downgrid Charging Platform}

Riding the Elevator: When a creature is inside the elevator, a loud warning pings, accompanied by an announcement for all organics: Aballon’s sun is dangerous at fullbright. Riding the elevator is safe, but stepping outside and onto the charging platform exposes a creature to the harsh, hot, unfiltered sunlight, which is harmful for most creatures (see @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00505locati.JournalEntryPage.05environmenta00]{Environment and Weather}).

Exploring the Area: A short corridor leads past the elevator to another set of automatic doors. The building beyond contains a forest of petrified trees. When examining them up close, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[mining-lore|dc:14] check or @Check[crafting|dc:16] check knows they are actually amethyst and jade pillars intricately carved to resemble petrified trees. A garden of statues is carved to resemble all sorts of creatures cavorting among the trees—anacites, graceful barathus, helpful skittermanders, magical beasts of lost Golarion, and creatures from planets at the other side of the galaxy. Finding the location tied to Tier-99-Professor’s identity marker is a laborious process of scanning with a comm unit, datapad, or similar computer while Searching the area. About an hour later, a PC using this method eventually confirms which cell is currently synced to Tier-99-Professor.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00504npcgal.JournalEntryPage.04shalalamula000]{Shalalamula} (jovial female seksaviak mystic) lives here with permission from the Insight Array and has free reign over her chosen living space, which she decorated with sculptures she created from polished minerals. Bins full of raw ore are stacked in untidy rows near a huge tumbler that constantly churns rough rocks in its belly and a potbellied stove heating a bubbling stewpot. Nearby, a few rough obsidian boulders form basic pews around a computer terminal where Shalalamula worships @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.deities.Item.OSQPUVZrtxJUisPa]{Triune}, weaving her own eccentric beliefs in with traditional doctrine.

Shalalamula knows exactly where Tier-99-Professor stored their data and shows the PCs if they ask her for help. She wasn’t on close terms with Tier-99-Professor, as Tierny was always either tired and in need of a recharge after a long day of work, or excited to begin a new workday and too busy to talk. Still, she respected Tierny’s dedication, and has noted their prolonged absence. She wasn’t present when Tierny died and is genuinely shocked if the PCs inform her of their demise.

About Anacites.name: About Anacites
About Anacites.text:
About Anacites

At this point, the PCs are likely to start asking questions in or out of character about anacites, their daily routines, and their society. Each PC may attempt a @Check[aballon-lore|dc:10|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge] or @Check[anacite-lore|dc:10|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge], or a @Check[society|dc:12|traits:concentrate,secret,skill,action:recall-knowledge|name:Recall Knowledge], to Recall Knowledge, or a @Check[diplomacy|dc:12|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information]. If a character succeeds, give the players @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout3000000]{Player Handout #3: Anacite Habits}.

On a critical success, a character also learns the location of the nearest charging platform and its basic layout (Downgrid Charging Platform, below). They also hear (or recall) a rumor that the local charging platform is considered to be an eccentric neighborhood by most of the local anacites.

GM Tip: Investigations.name: GM Tip: Investigations
GM Tip: Investigations.text:
GM Tip: Investigations

Throughout this adventure, the PCs investigate by succeeding at challenges incorporating skill checks, roleplay, or other exploration activities to find clues or leads. If the PCs fail at such a challenge, you might allow them to try again with help from a NPC, or perhaps a particularly close ally automatically succeeds at a task that falls within their area of expertise; for example, Ghellon might hear a rumor and give the PCs information they would have learned through Gather Information, or Erudite-Collaborator (see @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00502seeker.JournalEntryPage.02vendingservi00]{Here}) might help them troubleshoot technical difficulties.

Sometimes, failure has consequences described in the adventure. Sometimes failure simply means nothing happens. Success usually earns the party a clue, which might simply be information you read aloud, or could be a player handout you give to the player who discovered the clue.

Some players might enjoy hamming up a scene where everyone’s roleplaying a disastrous situation that “fails forward” in a comedic way. Others might prefer a challenging experience in which they feel the consequences of their failures, while some simply want to experience the story and make it their own. As the GM, you can ad lib additional consequences for critical failure, or rewards for critical success. Talk to your players about what kind of gaming experience they want to have. Remember, the goal is for everyone to have fun! Play the type of game you enjoy.

Getting on the Case.name: Getting on the Case
Getting on the Case.text:
Getting on the Case

A mystery is afoot, and it’s up to the PCs to solve it! They’ll do that by exploring locations and playing out scenes where they can find clues. Keep track of the clues the PCs find (or miss) using the @UUID[Actor.cW62Wu7ACCSptUZ7]{Evidence Tracker}. During the adventure, especially key moments in Chapter 2, the story advances in different ways depending on how many clues the PCs have discovered, or whether or not they discovered specific clues.

Going to the authorities at this stage results in a long wait for a brief virtual meeting with Prudent-Decision (inflexible agender anacite official), a stuffy anacite bureaucrat who explains that Tier-99-Professor hasn’t been reported missing, and is probably performing a task at their workplace, Polytechnica’s Central Files (see @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00502seeker.JournalEntryPage.02centralarchi00]{Here}), or resting at their @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00501coldca.JournalEntryPage.01downgridchar00]{Downgrid Charging Platform}. They suggest searching for Tier-99-Professor there. Sharing Tier-99-Professor’s holovid worries them, but they politely repeat that the PCs must follow protocols to “report an error” before the authorities will get involved.

If the PCs return to speak with Ghellon, she doesn’t know much about the drones or why they would attack. If they relay the scamps’ descriptions of “the man in the mask,” Ghellon confirms that Tierny’s new friend, the visiting professor, frequently wore a face mask. She thought little of it. “Hang around here a couple minutes and you’ll see a dozen far stranger things than a man in a mask.” Ghellon reiterates that the PCs might want to check out Tierny’s charging platform.

GM Tip: Rewards.name: GM Tip: Rewards
GM Tip: Rewards.text:
GM Tip: Rewards

Overcoming most encounters earns rewards, including equipment and experience that allow PCs to level up and upgrade their inventory. The PCs might not reach 2nd level until the end of this adventure, but you can use the GM Aid handout included with this adventure to track the XP they’re earning and items they’ve discovered to determine when they gain access to new powers.

Whenever the PCs defeat a creature in combat or bypass combat somehow (for example, through negotiation or coercing a surrender), they earn the amount of XP based on the challenge’s level in relation to their own, as indicated on the table in the inside back cover. Most encounters also contain Treasure, describing valuable items or useful gear, and Rewards, which include story XP and other special rewards.

Smog Alert.name: Smog Alert
Smog Alert.text:
Smog AlertTrivial or Moderate 1

The mysterious saboteur (@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00507aliens.JournalEntryPage.07campaignrole00]{Agent Z}) escapes, leaving the PCs to explore his abandoned hideout.

This ramshackle hideout seems out of place in the otherwise orderly megaplex. A lean-to made of a heavy tarp and the roof of an old autobus is wedged between the back stoops of a computer repair shop and recycling center. Trash, stained clothing, and food remnants litter the narrow alley. A thin bedroll peeks out from behind the tarp. Ashes from old fires sit in a metal drum nearby, but the makeshift camp was deserted some time ago, and thick tendrils of milky fog are starting to creep in.

Agent Z has used many hideouts across Striving; this is one of his more brazen ones, as it’s not especially secure, but he takes care not to spend too much time here. It’s out of sight of the city’s many security cameras, so Agent Z prefers this spot over some kind of formal dwelling with intrusive security measures.

If the PCs caught up with the drone, Agent Z flees into the alley and breaks a nearby air pump before fleeing the scene.

Failed Chase: If the PCs failed to catch up to the drone, Agent Z had additional time to prepare countermeasures. In addition to breaking the air pump even further, Agent Z waits around long enough to persuade the smog scamps that his pursuers (the PCs) are to blame. The scamps collect reinforcements, so the PCs face four smog scamps instead of just two.
