Staff are mostly anacites, androids, and SROs living in the utilitarian “ports” nestled alongside the curve of the main campus, with a few organic transplants visiting or assisting with research part-time while living in off-site apartments.

The PCs are free to explore Central Archives and browse the publicly accessible virtual library, which contains a preview of everything stored within the massive facility, but getting anywhere with their investigation requires authorizations visitors don’t have. Asking about the professor or poking around the campus gets Eruco’s attention. A short time after the PCs begin poking around, the friendly anacite invites the PCs down to vending services for a chat.

Striving Polytechnica.name: Striving Polytechnica
Striving Polytechnica.text:
Striving Polytechnica

High-speed automated trains connect Polytechnica’s scattered campuses, so it only takes a few minutes to get around. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[computers|dc:13|traits:exploration,skill,secret|name:Gather Information] or @Check[diplomacy|dc:13|traits:exploration,skill,secret,action:gather-information|name:Gather Information] learns that Tier-99-Professor worked at Polytechnica’s Central Archives alongside an assistant nicknamed Eruco.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.nO5b7gnQk3IiBabF.PlaylistSound.wF2Ab7D5QWCXDdaQ]{Striving Polytechnica}

Seekers in Striving.name: Seekers in Striving
Seekers in Striving.text:
Chapter 2: Seekers in Striving

At this point, the PCs know Tier-99-Professor’s shutdown was no accident, and they’ve encountered a mysterious figure who might be the murderer. Now their primary objective is to solve the mystery. Chapter 2 revolves around that investigation.

The PCs likely start by visiting Tierny’s workplace, Striving Polytechnica. If the party hesitates or gets stuck, NPCs they’ve already met encourage them to begin by querying Insight Array directly or visiting its headquarters at Central Circuit—this is also where they end up if they try to go to the authorities. If the PCs linger around the downgrid charging tower or return there, they encounter a dozen drones scuttling over the crime scene gathering evidence and running diagnostics. The drones ignore the PCs, redirecting all questions to Insight Array’s Processor facility in Central Circuit. The drones communicate in Trinary, which sounds like a baffling combination of beeps, static, and other electronic noises to the uninitiated.

Once the PCs visit these initial locations, they likely end up downloading the Insight Array comm unit app, which results in them receiving work assignments from the city’s officials. The PCs have a hidden enemy embedded in Striving’s government: @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00504npcgal.JournalEntryPage.04primefacilit00]{Prime-Facilitator}, who’s working to secure the transistor relic for their own purposes, and who gladly ties the PCs up with mundane tasks and risky “special assignments” in an effort to slow their investigation or (ideally) get them killed.

The PCs can approach the investigation however they like and search the locations presented in this chapter in any order. This investigation likely takes place over multiple days—allow the PCs to spend downtime as appropriate, to work mundane Insight Array jobs, and remember to intersperse the “special assignments” at appropriate times to keep the story moving and keep the tension high.

As the PCs find evidence and accomplish tasks, the GM should track this information in the @UUID[Actor.cW62Wu7ACCSptUZ7]{Evidence Tracker}. At the end of the chapter, Prime-Facilitator frames the PCs for the theft of the transistor relic, among other crimes. When they’re brought in for trial, the Machine Court’s judgment about the PCs’ innocence or guilt depends on how diligently they’ve been investigating up until now.

If the PCs need a place to rest, they can call on a friendly NPC. Shalalamula is happy to let them camp out among her sculptures, or Ghellon can call in a favor so they can crash for a while in a one-room apartment near Analog.

Continuing the Campaign.name: Continuing the Campaign
Continuing the Campaign.text:
Continuing the Campaign

After completing this adventure, your players should level up their characters to level 2 if they haven’t already. What happens next is up to you! They might continue adventuring on Aballon, such as by becoming freelance investigators or doing specialized work for Insight Array. They might continue Tier-99-Professor’s research by exploring First Ones sites on Aballon or by pursuing leads elsewhere in the galaxy.

One location ripe for further adventure is the planet Akiton. There, the PCs can team up with the Starfinder Society and explore the Wreck of the Returned in the Invasion’s Edge season of Starfinder Society Organized Play. In these adventures, they’ll explore the ship, discover ancient tech and magic, and contend with mysterious cultists, rival adventurers, and dangerous robots. The best place to start is Starfinder Society Scenario #1-01: Invasion’s Edge, in which the PCs can help establish a field base and explore debris from the Wreck of the Returned!

Facilitator’s Fate.name: Facilitator’s Fate
Facilitator’s Fate.text:
Facilitator’s Fate

Whatever happens to the relic and Agent Z, the PCs have a new enemy in Prime-Facilitator. If the PCs didn’t gather enough evidence in their investigation to prove their case, the anacite remains at the head of Striving’s bureaucracy. Though not individually powerful, Prime-Facilitator wields great influence through cunning manipulation behind the scenes and continues to plague and pester the PCs with meddlesome plots until they’ve finally left Aballon for good.

If the PCs gathered enough evidence to prove Prime-Facilitator’s guilt, the anacite is severed from their role in Striving’s bureaucracy. Officially, they’re deemed to have malfunctioned, and they’ve been recycled and repurposed; according to official records and the helpful Insight Array app, Prime-Facilitator no longer exists.

Relic’s Fate.name: Relic’s Fate
Relic’s Fate.text:
Relic’s Fate

If the PCs return the untampered transistor relic to Polytechnica, other ambitious anacites take up Tier-99-Professor’s sacred task and unravel the activation code. Their colleagues are abuzz with excitement months later when they activate the object—soon summoning godlike dimension-hopping entities who harvest all this reality’s energy for their vast energy requirements then shift realities as this existence collapses. In another reality, a different Agent Z tries again to save the world, endangering everyone around him in the process.

If the PCs help Agent Z deactivate or destroy the relic, or otherwise keep it hidden, they’ve prevented a dangerous First Ones incursion into their reality. For now, the PCs, their loved ones, and their entire existence is safe. Agent Z accepts whatever fate the PCs deem worthy; if brought to the Machine Court, they sentence him with deportation and exile from Aballon as a consequence of Tier-99-Professor’s death. The PCs are showered with renown and rewards for their role in solving the mysterious death of a beloved community figure. They might have earned an enduring enemy or an unpredictable ally in Agent Z and have made similar impressions on a host of other fascinating characters during their time in Aballon.

Conclusion.name: Conclusion
Conclusion.text:
Conclusion

The conclusion of the adventure should reflect the PCs’ choices as well as how effective their investigation was. The following conclusions are some examples of ways to wrap up this campaign and tie up loose ends based on what choices the PCs make, but feel free to invent your own endings—it’s your game!

Meet the Murderer.name: Meet the Murderer
Meet the Murderer.text:
Meet the Murderer

The murderer introduces himself as Agent Z, and if the PCs will listen, he passionately pleas for the PCs to destroy the relic, or at least let him take it far away from the machines who were built to activate it. He explains the danger of allowing it to be further studied, especially by someone like Prime-Facilitator, “who I foolishly underestimated and who will stop at nothing to use the device.”

Agent Z confesses to the murder and apologizes for the grief he’s caused them and others. He had been trying to convince Tier-99-Professor to let him attempt the delicate ritual to completely deactivate the relic for months, but the anacite refused to believe his theory and was unwilling to risk a precious piece of living history. Agent Z realized the two of them would never agree about the relic’s fate.

Nearly in tears, Agent Z admits that he wasn’t trying to kill Tierny—he believed the anacite had stored the relic in the cache, but was foiled one last time by his friend, who had hidden it in Archive 404 instead. When Agent Z and Prime-Facilitator learned where it was, Agent Z retrieved it—but by then, he knew of Prime-Facilitator’s intentions to kill everyone in the way of acquiring the device for foul purposes and fled to the Ice Wells instead of to his conniving “ally” in Striving.

He begs the PCs to let him destroy the relic and stop the First Ones from destroying this reality. If the PCs spend time talking him down, they might convince him to attempt a process to deactivate it without destroying it. The PCs must succeed at a Diplomacy check to convince him, or an Arcana or Crafting check to help him perform the task. If the PCs succeed at a check, Agent Z succeeds; if they fail both checks, the item is destroyed.

It’s possible the PCs don’t believe him, or don’t care. If they attack, Agent Z fights to the bitter end, even in his tortured and weakened state.

Rewards: Award the PCs 120 XP for meeting Agent Z. If they help Agent Z destroy the device, award XP as if they’d defeated him in combat.

Parting Shots.name: Parting Shots
Parting Shots.text:
Parting ShotsModerate 1

Hura and their guards hunker down inside for at least 10 minutes, giving the PCs time to rest and recover Focus Points. Eventually, they start firing the cannon again if the PCs didn’t already destroy it—they bring it back online if the PCs leave the area long enough for them to attempt repairs.

Parting ShotsModerate 1

@UUID[Actor.k9NEHmjUMWidKMJj]{Warlord Hura} @UUID[Actor.wKBAfpJlSeyBhtJy]{Sworn Blade of Shields} @UUID[Actor.LeqRQzLTZbAiohqi]{Sworn Blade of Sigils}

Creatures: Warlord Hura had been monitoring Agent Z for some time with a remote recording device introduced into his home. When Prime-Facilitator first heard of the jinsuls from Agent Z, the clever anacite agreed that they were a threat and that their accomplice should avoid them. Then, they secretly made contact with the jinsuls, knowing it could be useful to have dangerous “allies” to manipulate (or use as scapegoats). When Agent Z fled with the relic, Prime-Facilitator betrayed him in turn by tipping off the jinsuls. Warlord Hura’s forces attacked Agent Z when he was vulnerable—right after he stole the First Ones relic and had used up many of his powerful spells. He couldn’t handle the fight on his own and fell. Instead of killing him, the jinsuls decided to steal the relic and torture him until he admitted how to use it. They want to keep him alive, and they know the PCs are here searching for him thanks to their recording device; they use this fact against the PCs if they attempt to bargain, but they don’t intend to release such a valuable prisoner.

Inevitably, this scene breaks out into combat with the remaining jinsuls, who attack as soon as the PCs make threats, or as soon as the PCs seem like they’re going to flee the area for good. The fanatical jinsuls fight to the death.

Agent Z: Agent Z is safe inside the wrecked hull and escapes his restraints just as the battle ends. He exits the wreck bloodied and weak, but looking triumphant. He stops when he notices the PCs, and slowly raises an arm in greeting. He calls out in a calm voice, “What next? Got a minute to hear my side of the story?”

Wreck of the Condemned Prophet.name: Wreck of the Condemned Prophet
Wreck of the Condemned Prophet.text:
Wreck of the Condemned Prophet Moderate 1

Lost, severely weakened jinsuls repurposed the wreck of their small ship, the Condemned Prophet—which crashed into the side of the Ice Well after being spat out during the Drift Crash—into a command post for their “operations,” which mostly involve raiding supplies, killing local wildlife, and terrorizing local residents to make sure they stay out of their “territory.”

The broken hull of a dark gray, angular fighter craft juts out of the Ice Well’s rocky side. It’s sheared nearly in half and scorched by fire, but part of its hull is still intact. It’s shackled to the cliff face with articulated metal chains and peculiar purple symbols blaze in the air above the wreck.

This encounter uses the Ice Wells side of the flip-mat included with this adventure.

Terrain: The terrain outside the wreck is an ice field, and the cliff consists of a thick layer of perma-ice over rock. Climbing is treacherous without proper gear (@Check[athletics|dc:20|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb] to Climb), but movement speeds (including Climb) double while on the ice. At the end of each round, a creature who chooses to travel at increased speed must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:13] save to avoid slipping. On a failure, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for 1 round. On a critical failure, the creature falls @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. The jinsuls use the increased speed whenever possible, even at the risk of falling.

Wreck of the Condemned ProphetModerate 1

@UUID[Actor.9WnqrFwdytMw9PFN]{Particle Cannon} @UUID[Actor.rOyw0u1Qz2Srts9w]{Jinsul Lookouts (2)}

Hazard: The ship’s cannon is still operable. @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00507aliens.JournalEntryPage.07strandedjins00]{Warlord Hura} (cruel agender jinsul envoy) operates the cannon from inside, firing wildly to try to target as many PCs as possible.

Creatures: Two jinsul lookouts are always on patrol, and they attack as soon as the PCs approach. They fight to the death.

GM Tip: Running Jinsuls.name: GM Tip: Running Jinsuls
GM Tip: Running Jinsuls.text:
GM Tip: Running Jinsuls

In Starfinder, some enemies can be reasoned with or persuaded to switch sides, but some villains hate the PCs (or one of their affiliations), want to kill them, and won’t stop trying until they’re incapacitated or dead.

In this adventure, the jinsul invaders in the following encounters play that role, a “punchable face” for the players to fight and not feel sorry for, because they truly mean the PCs harm and will stop at nothing to make it happen. The invaders, who are jinsuls from the Scoured Stars stranded here after the Drift Crisis, have fanatical beliefs and were psychologically conditioned from birth to hate every creature that isn’t either another jinsul or blessed by their god Kadrical. Jinsuls can’t be talked into a fair trade or truce. They might surrender if odds are steeply against them, but only if they can keep their dignity and freedom intact.

If that type of story doesn’t appeal to your group, you can change it.

Abaddon Fields.name: Abaddon Fields
Abaddon Fields.text:
Abaddon Fields

The lowest level of Teardrop Ice Well is a mile-wide expanse of dark, severely cold ice fields. Barren stretches of rock rise from the ice. Satellite imagery doesn’t penetrate this deep and few explorers return from this zone, so little is known about its geography or denizens. Recent reports say it’s a frozen wasteland ruled by cruel warlords who harvest their lands and its creatures as though they were meaningless grist for a mill.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[aballon-lore|dc:13], @Check[history-lore|dc:13], or @Check[scoured-stars-lore|dc:13] checks knows that at one time this deep habitat teemed with flora and fauna—at the time, Abaddon Fields was an ironic name, chosen as a snide joke to contrast the idyllic twilight beauty of the cenote’s depths. Xenowardens fought hard to prevent greedy corporate agents and nosy explorers from disturbing the delicate ecosystems in Abaddon Fields, spreading rumors of dangerous organisms and lobbying with the Machine Court for strict regulations surrounding travel to the Ice Wells. The cause picked up public approval, and all but a few naysayers joined the wave to keep Aballon’s Ice Wells green. The movement was a success.

Then a party of jinsul invaders moved in after getting stranded on-world during the Drift Crisis. The callous raiders indiscriminately exterminated “pests”—their word for naturally occurring plants and animals—while clearing the land. They constructed a covert outpost and decimated the ecosystem in days—before Xenowardens even detected their presence.

Some Xenowardens with bonds to the planet had felt the disturbance but didn’t have details about its source until it was too late. If the PCs ask, the Xenowardens agree to provide a reward for driving the invaders out of Teardrop Ice Well at the GM’s discretion.

Obstacle: First, the PCs must find the raider outpost by searching a mile of virtually identical landscape that’s constantly being swept over with snow that obscures footprints.

Finding the Raider OutpostObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[arcana|dc:13], @Check[occultism|dc:13], or @Check[religion|dc:13] to detect the residue of powerful magical rituals; @Check[survival|dc:14] to follow tracks; @Check[piloting|dc:14] to navigate; an appropriate item or spell overcomes this obstacle.

A flat landscape of white stretches out, dappled with pools of frozen water mirroring the steely sky. Everything blurs together as snow begins to flurry and the ice field stretches out with only a few landmarks—a collection of boulders, a petrified stump, and endless configurations of frozen lakes.

If two PCs overcome this obstacle, or any PC critically succeeds at overcoming it, the party finds the raider outpost after [[/r 1d4]] hours. Otherwise, the search takes nearly a full day, and each character who failed their check is demoralized by the oppressive landscape, taking a –2 penalty to initiative rolls in future battles in Aballon Fields until they’ve spent at least 8 hours resting outside the Ice Well (@UUID[Item.eXgKXwjRVgYPIIKb]{Oppressive Landscape}).

The Gloaming.name: The Gloaming
The Gloaming.text:
The Gloaming Moderate 1

The PCs must travel for a few hours through the Gloaming to reach Agent Z’s location, and their journey takes them through more of the Ice Wells’ dangers.

Obstacle: This deep fungal forest forms a gloomy understory beneath the canopy. Nearly all light is blocked, with a few pale shafts straggling into the murk and creating dim illumination for 6 hours of the day. The other 6 hours are complete darkness. Items and spells that create light are less effective in the Gloaming, casting light at half their normal range and half its normal brightness, and characters with any form of darkvision can only see half as far as normal as their vision is clouded by the deep murkiness.

Persistent GloomObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[arcana|dc:15] to counteract the unorthodox magic plaguing the area, @Check[occultism|dc:15] to purge the area of unclean psychic energies causing the darkness to linger, @Check[religion|dc:15] to bless the space.

If at least two characters succeed, or one PC critically succeeds, the darkening effects of the Gloaming temporarily recede, allowing the PCs to see normally for 24 hours. If they remain in the area for longer than that time period, they must overcome the persistent gloom again.

Scene Notes Macro

@UUID[Macro.ELotS5eg49qX2PLA]{Reveal Dewblossom}

Reveals the Dewblossom token, while hiding the tile on the @UUID[Scene.NljaYtpj8rIAiWuQ]{The Gloaming} Scene.

The GloamingModerate 1

@UUID[Actor.QWALSV8WnUxsnjlp]{Dewblossom} @UUID[Actor.aY0mgYa6E9BFrojd]{Shroomclaws (2)}

Hazard: As the PCs travel through the Gloaming, they stumble across an area inhabited by a dangerous plant called a dewblossom.

Creatures: The shroomclaws that stalked the PCs in Day Delve return to haunt their footsteps in the growing murk of the Gloaming. Two shroomclaws ambush the PCs when they stumble on the dewblossom. If the PCs befriended the young injured shroomclaw, these shroomclaws don’t attack them, instead harrying the dewblossom with attacks in an effort to protect the PCs. In this event, award the group XP as though they’d defeated the shroomclaws in battle.

Development: The dewblossom doesn’t fight to the death if its meal (or allies) put up a struggle, but it defends itself if attempts are made to cut the victim out of it. If PCs continue attacking the dewblossom after these conditions are met, it vomits up the dead character’s body and curls into its bud form, which has layers of tough bark-like leaves and thorny spines sticking out in every direction. Killing the dewblossom might damage the local ecosystem (@Check[nature|dc:12] or @Check[survival|dc:12] check) but also eliminates a dangerous predator that’s killed other explorers in the past.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.VGtXw1ww0jZFKSVp]{Ruined Backpack}
A ruined backpack with a bright orange kerchief tied to it lies forgotten among the detritus around the dewblossom. This 4-compartment denim bag contains a pastel pink steel thermos with a Strawberry Machine Cake motif (empty), soggy R2E rations, a flashlight, a commercial glow up spell amp, a tactical medpatch, and a glamer projector.

The smallest pocket contains a comm unit belonging to Jeotanni (capricious nonbinary pahtra adventurer), an explorer who came to Akiton to explore the Ice Wells, according to their social media presence. She’s not relevant to the PCs’ investigation, but if they look her up, give them @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout2000000]{Handout #20: Jeotanni’s Comm Unit Contents}.

What Do You Do?.name: What Do You Do?
What Do You Do?.text:
What Do You Do?

The characters (and their players) have an important choice to make. They might decide to rescue the probable murderer—the person they’ve been hunting and who’s foiled them time and again—and end the cycle of violence, or they can get revenge. They might leave the murderer to their fate and move on with their lives, perhaps dealing with the jinsuls for fame, fortune, or as a favor to the locals. This might be a tough choice for some players, and many groups might be divided, so be sure to allow ample time for the group to discuss their options in and out of character. Don’t rush the moment! In fact, now might be a great time for a snack break.

The PCs can use the abandoned hideout as a new base camp. It’s sheltered from the elements and in a relatively secret, remote location that’s perfect for stashing valuables, resting up, or taking time to craft on the fly. The PCs can establish the hideout as their new base camp, but you should make it clear that the suspected murderer’s fate is urgently in the balance as long as he’s in jinsul raiders’ claws.

Where’s the Murderer?.name: Where’s the Murderer?
Where’s the Murderer?.text:
Where’s the Murderer?

The suspect might be missing, but the case is all but closed. However, there’s a troubling pop-up on the laptop: a security alert. A hacked wingbot is frantically pinging in with a live security feed, which the PCs can view on the laptop. At first, they catch a few motion shots of the Ice Well’s landscape, then the feed focuses on a hooded humanoid figure wearing a mask (Agent Z). They’re clutching their side and casting a spell as a monstrous, six-limbed alien with blades grafted to each of its powerful legs skitters toward their position. A quickly unleashed spell blasts the monster back, but two more are charging at the lone fighter, and the figure stumbles before the attacker’s shining blades. Kneeling now, with a blade resting on either side of their neck. A garble of sound indicates speech as the attackers communicate.

The drone transmits the approximate location, since satellite imaging doesn’t reliably work inside an Ice Well. The attack occurred down a zone in the Gloaming.

Gathering Evidence.name: Gathering Evidence
Gathering Evidence.text:
Gathering Evidence

A laptop sits on top of a wooden crate, charging from a portable generator. The laptop’s password protected (@Check[computers|dc:15|action:hack|name:Hack]; the PCs can try multiple times or seek an ally’s aid if needed). If the PCs access the laptop, give them @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout1800000]{Handout #18: Laptop Entry 1} and @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout1900000]{Handout #19: Laptop Entry 2}; the laptop contains incontrovertible proof of Agent Z’s guilt.

First Ones Theory: The file that’s currently open is a thesis about the First Ones’ true purpose in returning to this reality—to use it as fuel for their interdimensional journeys—backed up with complex technomagical diagrams and equations showing extrapolated uses of recovered First Ones technology. The essay mentions research taken from sites on Arshalin, Aballon, and Lajok, with a recent addendum about Akiton.

Investigation: All journal entries are signed “Agent Z” and there’s no way to further identify the author, though they clearly confess to the murder of Tier-99-Professor. The journal describes how he created the memorial out of guilt for ending such a fascinating individual’s life and was touched to see it grow as others added to it. He describes wanting to apologize to Tier-99-Professor’s colleagues and friends but knows that admitting his guilt too early might ruin his plan.

Additional evidence on the laptop includes long-distance images taken of the professor, illicitly obtained plans of Archive 404 and information about each of the PCs, unsigned communication logs with an anonymous inside source in Central Circuit (Prime-Facilitator), and more. It’s enough to exonerate the PCs if they’re still facing any accusations in Striving and to provide further evidence of Prime-Facilitator’s involvement.

Security Logs: The laptop’s security logs mention jinsul activity in other zones of the Ice Well, and that Agent Z spotted raiders testing his perimeter while reviewing security footage. A recent security camera feed shows a distressing video, foreshadowing the live scene broadcast by the wingbot: in this short vid, a six-limbed trooper tears through the door, which is clearly electrified judging by the arcs of electricity jolting the trooper’s hulking, spiky body. The door is almost completely destroyed when the trooper collapses, convulsing. Two six-limbed beings in similar attire arrive quickly to administer aid, then the feed cuts as one shoots the camera with its firearm.

Listening Device: A PC using @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic}, or one who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:15] check, notices a minuscule angular gray device about the size of a pebble stuck to a pipe in the ceiling. Its design is totally alien, and it appears to be sticking to the surface through some sort of molecular magnetism, but a PC who succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:17] check or @Check[scoured-stars-lore|dc:14] check identifies it as jinsul manufacture. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:14] or @Check[computers|dc:14] check determines the object is a bug—a live recording device that transmits sound and video to a remote location. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[arcana|dc:16] or @Check[computers|dc:16] check can trace the signal to the Abaddon Fields and the rough location of the @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03wreckoftheco00]{Wreck}.

Rewards: Award the PCs 40 XP if they access the laptop’s records and 20 XP if they find the listening device.

Murderer’s Hideout.name: Murderer’s Hideout
Murderer’s Hideout.text:
Murderer’s Hideout

A door opens in the rock. Smooth, marble steps completely out of place inside the ice-rimed rock pit—almost as if they were ripped from another world—descend 20 feet to a frigid hallway of bare gray stone. A heavy airlock door hangs open, leading to a one-room survival bunker.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.nvRW2tK8x9GsnDEm]{Supplies} @UUID[Actor.MHYVyjfM5IyOCQMZ]{Rickety Table}
The cramped space is packed with steel shelves stacked with supplies (mostly canned rations and jugs of filtered water), a chemalyzer, an explorer’s canteen, a tactical hypopen, 4 medpatches, and an emergency beacon. The crude furniture is crowded around a rickety card table stacked with various types of ammunition and a commercial laser pistol disassembled on it. A character can put it back together in working order with a successful @Check[crafting|dc:13] check. There’s also a commercial plasma sword with what looks like a stylized Z engraved in the hilt.

Transistor Relic: @UUID[Actor.XOgjzGLnFO3UCaHw]{Behind Mattress}
Concealed behind a bare mattress leaning up against the wall is a commercial null space chamber in the corner containing a few copies of vintage racing magazines and the missing transistor relic. Give the players @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout1700000]{Handout #17: Relic Scan}. Without extensive knowledge of how it works, not to mention a well-funded laboratory, the PCs have little chance of making use of the First Ones relic, but they may decide to return it to the university, the authorities, or even Agent Z.

Rewards: Award the PCs 120 XP for recovering the relic.

Last Goodbye.name: Last Goodbye
Last Goodbye.text:
Last Goodbye

Biting wind howls over the precipice of this steep cliff—a ledge of jagged rock is the only barrier to the abyss below. A few yards from the ledge, sheltered by some thorny shrubs with sweet blue berries, a gentler slope is partly obscured behind a boulder painted with a strange symbol.

Discover Hidden TruthObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[survival|dc:14] to find and follow tracks; @Check[perception|dc:15] to spot an outline in the rock or a patch of melted snow; @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic} to discover entrance; @Check[arcana|dc:15], @Check[occultism|dc:15], or @Check[religion|dc:15] to recognize @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.deities.Item.N1eCNDynvJFIl154]{Eloritu} rune painted on a nearby boulder.

A hidden door carved into the cliff face about fifteen feet down from its peak is accessible via a narrow, unstable rope bridge, marked by an invisible holy rune of Eloritu painted onto a rock beside it. The rune is revealed when @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic} or any other spell is cast within 30 feet of it. Drawing one of the other runes (@Check[religion|dc:16]; a worshipper of Eloritu can bypass this check) causes the outline of the door to appear in violet light. Creatures can now see the door and access the Puzzle Lock.

Puzzle LockObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[crafting|dc:14] to disable the locking mechanism; @Check[arcana|dc:14], @Check[occultism|dc:14] or @Check[religion|dc:14] to decipher the pattern using clues from Eloritu’s divine symbology to extrapolate a theoretical sixth rune; @Check[perception|dc:14] to align the pattern through trial and error. Two successes are needed to open the door.

Failure: The PCs might fail to overcome these obstacles and be unable to bypass the lock at this time. In that event, they might choose to follow the tracks deeper into the Ice Well (proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03thegloaming000]{The Gloaming}). They might instead retreat to seek assistance. If you want to keep the adventure moving, you might allow the PCs another attempt, but penalize them for failures, such as by reducing the amount of equipment they find in the hideout, or having wildlife (such as sharpwings) attack them as they try to access the puzzle lock again. Whatever you decide, don’t let a few failed checks cause the adventure to grind to a halt.

Canopy.name: Canopy
Canopy.text:
Canopy

This frosty rainforest grows on tiered cliffs that slope downward toward the bottom of the Ice Wells. The atmosphere is normal here, rich with oxygen exhaled by the pristine forest.

Hunting SharpwingsObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[athletics|dc:13] or @Check[acrobatics|dc:13] to block an incoming attack, @Check[stealth|dc:12] to hide, @Check[survival|dc:14] to create camouflage, @Check[nature|dc:14] to repel the sharpwing or lure it away.

A massive shape blots out the rays of light filtering down from above—a mature sharpwing screeches as it spots new prey, turning into a sharp dive! Any creature who fails to overcome the obstacle takes @Damage[1d4[slashing]] damage from the sharpwing’s claws as it swoops at them.

If fewer than two PCs succeed, the PCs are attacked by a pair of young @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00507aliens.JournalEntryPage.07sharpwing00000]{Sharpwings}!

Climb Steep WallsObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[athletics|dc:13|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb] to Climb down, @Check[acrobatics|dc:12] to rappel down, @Check[crafting|dc:15] to rig a belay system.

Cliff faces form rugged steps on a giant’s scale, covered with trees and vines. A creature who fails to overcome the obstacle becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} after the climb. Luckily, creatures who critically fail to overcome this hazard get tangled in thick vines and branches, and avoid plummeting hundreds of feet into darkness.

Track Down LeadsObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[survival|dc:15] to find and follow tracks, @Check[perception|dc:12] to spot destruction in the surrounding landscape, @Check[society|dc:15] to identify boot prints worn by Pact Worlds humanoids, @Check[society|dc:15] to recognize jinsul blade scuffs.

The PCs discover a trail of boot prints that lead to a ledge atop a jagged cliff (see @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03lastgoodbye000]{Last Goodbye}).

It’s difficult to notice other tracks in the thick undergrowth, but if at least two PCs succeed, or one PC critically succeeds, they notice signs of laser fire and more scrapes and scuffs from jinsul leg blades. Many laser blasts are concentrated near the boulder; the scrapes and scuffs lead deeper into the Ice Well.

Rewards: Award the PCs 20 XP for reaching Last Goodbye.

Day Delve.name: Day Delve
Day Delve.text:
Day Delve

Silvery grass grows thick beneath gnarled trees with drooping canopies of blue and white flowers, some of which have ripened into sweet berries. Icy waterfalls sparkle along the cavern walls, trickling into shallow pools full of mossy stones.

To navigate deeper into the Ice Wells, the PCs need to overcome environmental obstacles and avoid dangerous creatures. Each PC should attempt a single skill check to overcome any given obstacle; while they make progress through the Ice Wells regardless of their check results, the check results determine additional discoveries (or dangers) the PCs may encounter. Grant the PCs bonuses to their checks for the use of appropriate equipment or spells. These obstacles each represent multiple hours, even days, of exploration at the GM’s discretion.

Track Down LeadsObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[survival|dc:13] to find and follow tracks, @Check[perception|dc:12] to spot destruction in the surrounding landscape, @Check[society|dc:12] to identify boot prints of the type commonly worn by Pact Worlds humanoids, @Check[society|dc:14] to recognize jinsul blade scuffs.

If at least two PCs succeed at their checks, or any PC critically succeeds, the PCs can follow the blade scuffs to an area of churned earth that’s oddly bare of moss or other flora. Buried two feet down is a steel lockbox of an unusual, brutalist design (@UUID[Actor.vDnYwcAC8aOzWV59]{Steel Lockbox}). All the items inside have a similarly strange aesthetic but function as the following items: an autograppler, a climbing kit, a commercial plasma cannon with 100 charges, a suit of commercial aegis series armor, and a commando serum. With a successful @Check[society|dc:16], or @Check[scoured-stars-lore|dc:14], a PC identifies the items as manufactured by jinsuls, a viciously intolerant group of violent zealots from a region of distant space called the Scoured Stars.

Hunting Shroomclaw PackObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[deception|dc:13] or @Check[survival|dc:13] to evade tracking pursuers, @Check[stealth|dc:14] to hide from the predators, @Check[nature|dc:14] to tame an injured shroomclaw.

Off-putting shapes and sounds caught in glimpses solidify into a real threat: a pack of predators is stalking the group. Any creature who fails to overcome the obstacle is singled out and attacked by a shroomclaw, taking @Damage[(1d6+3)[piercing]] damage before the predator scampers away into the thick undergrowth.

If at least two PCs succeed at their checks, or any PC critically succeeds, the group notices one of the younger shroomclaws lingering behind the pack. This shroomclaw is limping from an obvious injury, and it’s tamable with patience and offerings of food. The first time a PC feeds it, the injured shroomclaw follows the party at a distance, appearing at dawn and dusk and only allowing the person who fed it to approach, though it quickly adapts to anyone else who feeds it. After the third feeding it begins guarding camp, warning the PCs of unusual activity and even defending the PCs from attacks. It stops limping after a few days or sooner with prompt medical care.

If fewer than two PCs succeed, the PCs are attacked by a pair of @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00507aliens.JournalEntryPage.07shroomclaw0000]{Shroomclaws}.

Treacherous DropObstacle 1

Overcome @Check[athletics|dc:14|traits:move,skill,action:climb|name:Climb] to Climb down the cliff face, @Check[acrobatics|dc:14] to rappel down, @Check[crafting|dc:15] to rig a pulley system.

A sheer cliff face is slick with spray from a nearby waterfall and has frozen to a sheen of ice in the subzero temperatures. A creature who fails to overcome the obstacle becomes fatigued after the climb. A creature who critically fails also falls 20 feet and takes @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]] damage—but at least they made it all the way down.

Rewards: Award the PCs 20 XP for handling these obstacles and reaching Canopy.

Base Camp.name: Base Camp
Base Camp.text:
Base Camp

This cozy lodge is built of petrified wood ethically harvested from Canopy below. The hearth and dining hall take up most of the cabin’s first story, with a pantry and staircase in the back. Upstairs is a set of partitioned bunks and pallets surrounding a hearth, where guests have an open invitation to stay.

Creatures: @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00504npcgal.JournalEntryPage.04springfrost000]{Spring Shoots Emerging Through Frost} (happy-go-lucky male khizar xenodruid) is expecting the PCs to show up and has prepared for them. When they arrive, he’s waiting in the base camp’s dining hall, having already prepared fresh-baked cookies and mugs of hot spice tea for them.

Spring Frost knows a lot about the Ice Well’s various habitats and is eager to share that knowledge while his guests enjoy refreshments and rest. He can help prepare them for their expedition, explaining the need for warm clothes, rappelling tools, camping gear, and rations—and offering these items for sale at fair prices. He’s willing to answer questions about the flora and fauna in the Ice Well, as well as the intrusive jinsul presence, which he believes is getting worse. If the PCs ask about “Zirem” (or someone fitting Agent Z’s description), Spring Frost doesn’t know much, aside from the fact that Zirem is an explorer from offworld who frequently spends days at a time in Striving before making short visits to the Ice Wells.

Wilderness Survival

The final chapter of this adventure rips the PCs away from the metal city and launches them into a wilderness expedition deep below Aballon’s surface. The PCs are free to return to Striving if they need supplies but should be able to trade for most necessities at Frost Lookout. They should feel an urgency to keep exploring and might decide to live off the land or look for enterprising ways to earn credits when they return from their “camping trip.”

Foraging For Food: The PCs might need to forage for edible food or choose to live off the land to spare supplies. In their downtime, a PC can Subsist using Survival as normal. Other PCs can Aid this check using Life Science Lore or Nature.

Environment: For details on cold weather and other environmental dangers, see Starfinder GM Core.

Shop: Spring Frost shares his bountiful resources with those truly in need and sells the rest in a small canteen-style shop inside his cabin. The shop has everything required for exploring the Ice Wells, including climbing kits, camping kits, cable line, rations, and other common tech items up to level 2. He can special order an item he doesn’t have in stock upon request (such as magic or medical items), which takes 1 day for drone delivery from Striving.

If the PCs want Spring Frost to accompany them into the Ice Well or help them beyond giving advice, they can hire him as a guide for 50 credits per day. He’s a pacifist and prefers to avoid danger skillfully (his Skills include [[/r 1d20+8]]{Nature +8}, [[/r 1d20+6]]{Perception +6}, and [[/r 1d20+6]]{Survival +6}). The PCs don’t need to Subsist if they hire a guide.

Treasure: @UUID[Actor.jqkMlcz7hDEuNAo4]{Spring Frost's Homemade Kit}
Spring Frost gives each PC a homemade kit that contains the following: a downloadable guide that helps identify edible plants and fungus (+2 item bonus to Nature or Survival checks to identify, harvest, or Recall Knowledge about plants and fungus in the Ice Well), homemade trail mix (counts as 3 days of rations for 1 Medium or Large creature), explorer’s bandages (2 commercial medpatches), and an air bubble spell gem.

Earning Income: Ghellon, Enaria, and Remena are willing to buy wild ingredients the PCs harvest from the Ice Well. A PC might use Nature, Survival, or Life Science Lore to identify and harvest the herbs. This should be a secret check that the PCs don’t know about until Enaria’s payment. The first time they critically fail, Ghellon stops purchasing from them, but Enaria states that while she should be angry the PCs tried to sell her poison, whatever they picked is about to be the next Nightarch fad!

Frost Lookout.name: Frost Lookout
Frost Lookout.text:
Frost Lookout

A precarious ramp with no railing hugs the dull blue ice shaft as it winds down into the pit, offering dizzying views of radial layers of frost-crusted greenery spiraling down into darkness. Frigid wind whistles up from the deep, carrying the odor of slow decay and fragrant wood.

Most expeditions into the Ice Well meet here, and a few scattered tents and firepits surround the outskirts of the largest structure in the area—a cabin that looks like it’s made of petrified wood (see Base Camp below). A few satellite shacks and tents huddle a few yards away from the main cabin.

On this level, frost rimes the ground every night, but temperatures are on the cool side of normal most of the time. Unless the PCs arrive at night, most of the tents are deserted while their occupants delve the Ice Well.

Teardrop Ice Well.name: Teardrop Ice Well
Teardrop Ice Well.text:
Teardrop Ice Well

The Teardrop Ice Well is so named for its graduated, upturned funnel shape. The cenote’s surface opening is 30 feet across, but the lowest chamber of the cave system stretches nearly a mile wide at its lowest depth of 2,047 feet below the surface. Explorers classify the Ice Well’s locations into zones based on light levels, weather patterns, and wildlife. Most creatures in the upper levels (Upper Lookout, Day Delve, and Canopy) are photosynths and herbivores, but the lower levels have a more vicious ecosystem full of predators, scavengers, and omnivores who will eat anything that fits in their orifices. Sometimes dangerous creatures hunt as high up as Day Delve, but they typically don’t target larger creatures (such as the PCs) unless their prey is injured or alone. If the PC inquire or look up information about the Ice Wells give them @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout1300000]{"Handout #13: About Ice Wells"}.

Scene Notes Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.nO5b7gnQk3IiBabF.PlaylistSound.ld4MKO9ABDLBBWsB]{Teardrop Ice Well}

@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03frostlookout00]{Frost Lookout:} Named for the base camp built by Spring Shoots Emerging Through Frost (see @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03basecamp000000]{Here}), this wide inner lip juts out like a shelf from the northwestern side of the cenote 328 feet down. Frost Lookout is accessible by a steep, dizzying staircase carved into the rock. Many expeditions camp here between delves, as it’s relatively sheltered and safe from weather and wildlife. Temperatures range from normal to mild cold.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03daydelve000000]{Day Delve:} This lush frost tundra is filled with evergreen trees that grow delicious berries. Edible plants are plentiful here, with new discoveries being made frequently. Most wildlife is docile, and temperatures range from mild cold to normal.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03canopy00000000]{Canopy:} This is a tiered deep forest. Gloomy, but light filters down here. Wildlife is often avoidant but can be dangerous. Temperatures are mild cold. This zone and all zones below have a normal atmosphere due to thick vegetation.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03lastgoodbye000]{Last Goodbye:} This narrow cliff juts dramatically from the northern side of the Ice Well, too precarious and windblown to serve as more than a landmark. It has mild cold temperatures.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03thegloaming000]{The Gloaming:} This region has only a few hours of very gloomy light each day, attracting fungi and creatures that are more active in the dark. Sharpwings roost here in the dangerous and severe cold. “Blizzards” caused by snowfall from the laden canopy above begin when winds are high, more commonly on the north side.

@UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00503frozen.JournalEntryPage.03abaddonfield00]{Abaddon Fields:} At the deepest part of the Ice Well, ice fields stretch out in total darkness. At one time, this deep habitat teemed with flora and fauna, then jinsul invaders moved in and exterminated the “pests” as part of constructing their covert outpost. Even before vicious xenophobic aliens invaded it, Teardrop’s lowest zone was extremely dangerous. Temperatures are severe cold and blizzards are common.

Frozen Heart of Aballon.name: Frozen Heart of Aballon
Frozen Heart of Aballon.text:
Chapter 3: Frozen Heart of Aballon

The final phase of the PCs’ investigation takes them to a remote nature preserve outside the bustling metal city. The Teardrop Ice Well is one of the planet’s pristine micro-ecosystems found in the wilderness northeast of Striving, just south of the Sea of Glass.

No high speed transportation infrastructure connects to that location, but a private planetary shuttle can reach the location in roughly 45 minutes—the PCs likely know a wealthy VIP or well-connected bartender who can hook them up.

Without a shuttle, the journey overland takes 3 hours in a vehicle or one day on foot trekking across smooth craters picked clean by automated harvesters, rocky gray crags jutting up from the ground, and gravelly off-road paths.

Aballon’s atmosphere is thin outside Striving; creatures that aren’t acclimated become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} after a few hours. At the end of each day, creatures who aren’t acclimated must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:14] save to determine how their body is adapting to the thin atmosphere. Acclimation requires the PCs to succeed at their saves for three consecutive days (a critical success counts as two days worth of successes). Therefore, some PCs likely acclimate in a few days, and others might need a week or more to adjust. Using magic or tech to breathe can suppress fatigue or prevent the need for a check, but using such a method doesn’t help them acclimate to the atmosphere.

Tier-99-Professor.name: Tier-99-Professor
Tier-99-Professor.text:
Tier-99-Professor

Fondly called Tierny (eccentric agender anacite technomancer) by their close colleagues and friends, Tier-99-Professor was a respected anacite scholar who specialized in technologies built by the First Ones, the ancient progenitor culture of the anacite species. Until their recent death after an unexpected shutdown caused by foul play, they worked at Striving Polytechnica, where they earned their reputation as one of the most respected and accomplished experts in their field.

Special: Tierny mentored countless students, visitors, and fresh colleagues over their long years at Polytechnica’s Archives. Posthumously, a message reached some of their allies and called for their help.

Spring Frost.name: Spring Frost
Spring Frost.text:
Spring Frost

Spring Frost (happy-go-lucky male khizar xenodruid) is amused by the ironic nickname he’s been carelessly given. His full name is Spring Shoots Emerging Through Frost, a hopeful name symbolizing renewal and perseverance, but “spring frost” is a common khizar idiom for a sudden inconvenience or tragedy that appears out of nowhere.

Spring Frost is a solitary Xenowarden charged with protecting the Teardrop Ice Well’s ecosystems. He spends most of his time at Base Camp or guiding expeditions to Day Delve and Canopy. Spring Frost enjoys ice fishing and eagerly shows explorers his favorite spots.

Adventure Role: Spring Frost’s Base Camp is a safe place for the PCs to rest and resupply. He provides roleplay opportunities and can help if the player characters are lacking sufficient wilderness survival skills.

Making an Impression: Anyone who can impress him with a fishing story (@Check[deception|dc:15|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression] or @Check[performance|dc:15|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression]) or a great catch (@Check[nature|dc:12|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression] or @Check[survival|dc:12|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression]) improves his attitude by one step. Littering or carelessly harming the Ice Well’s natural resources changes his attitude to unfriendly or decreases it by one step if he was already friendly or helpful.

Ally Benefits: Spring Frost guides for his friends at discounted rates (25 credits per day if friendly, 10 if helpful). He provides sustenance for anyone he’s friendly toward, meaning they don’t have to Subsist.

Shalalamula.name: Shalalamula
Shalalamula.text:
Shalalamula

Shalalamula (jovial female seksaviak mystic) traveled to Aballon from Kazmurg’s Absurdity, a distant sector of space. Seksaviaks are Large-sized vertebrates with six limbs that they can use as hands or feet, with long tubular bodies covered in fur (see Galaxy Guide 60).

Shalalamula’s offbeat faith inspired her to go on a religious pilgrimage to Striving to commune with Epoch’s neural network as part of her worship of Triune. Insight Array is curious about beings from the Absurdity, having never encountered them before, and is meticulously studying Shalalamula (with her consent) while she learns about Striving.

She invites anyone she meets to worship with her and tries to involve them in a respectful discussion about their religious and philosophical views, explaining her belief that Triune’s All-Code encompasses everything, forming a vast simulation that people perceive as the multiverse. Shalalamula believes the Gap was Triune’s attempt to prevent mass panic in a divine reboot because too many people suddenly discovered the truth and tried to escape the simulation. She also believes pop culture divinity @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.deities.Item.o9dgag7sAiFUnN9I]{Lambatuin} is an aspect of Triune who’s trying to expose mortals to the truth using popular memes and media tropes. She calls her faith All-Codism.

Adventure Role: Shalalamula is a lighthearted character who provides fun roleplay opportunities or moments of comic relief. She’s not an important player in the investigation, but might help her friends out with useful spells or mystical insight.

Making an Impression: Shalalamula’s attitude begins as indifferent. Attending one of her worship sessions or engaging in respectful discussion improves her attitude by one step. PCs can improve her attitude in this way once per week.

Ally Benefits: +1 circumstance bonus to one Occultism or Religion check per day (friendly), one 4th-rank or lower divine spell per week (helpful).

Prime-Facilitator.name: Prime-Facilitator
Prime-Facilitator.text:
Prime-Facilitator

The anacite designated Prime-Facilitator (callous agender anacite bureaucrat) is secretly working to frame the PCs and stop their investigation. Yet as a powerful figure known for their unerring service and rational assessments of difficult situations, no one suspects such a betrayal from them. Months ago, a mysterious visitor shared a grim truth with Prime-Facilitator, presenting evidence that the First Ones burn suns as fuel and can shift dimensions by using whole realities as fodder. Initially, Prime-Facilitator decided to betray Insight Array and their own programming, telling themselves it was to save the Universe. But since learning of the power of the First Ones’ devices, Prime-Facilitator has harbored secret desires to use them to advance their own goals, which deviate further from those of Insight Array with every passing day.

Prime-Facilitator secretly and efficiently helped Agent Z carry out his plan to steal more relics, loaning him drones, helping him conceal his activities, and even suggesting he hide out in an Ice Well (despite knowing about the presence of dangerous jinsuls in the area). Prime-Facilitator made sure all of Tierny’s reports of anomalous activity weren’t properly investigated and continues to assist Agent Z under the pretense of working together, but fully intends to find a way to get Agent Z out of the way for good—and deal with the player characters as well—once the transistor device is in their possession.

Special: Prime-Facilitator puts on a friendly facade if the PCs meet them before the Machine Court trial, but their attitude toward the PCs doesn’t change even if they are polite, respectful, and try to impress the anacite. Prime-Facilitator intends to carry out their plan no matter what, and can’t be swayed. The first time the PCs look up Prime-Facilitator, give them @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00509hando1.JournalEntryPage.09handout1200000]{Handout #12: Public Profile: Prime-Facilitator}.

Hesop.name: Hesop
Hesop.text:
Hesop

Hesop (anxious male damaya lashunta bureaucrat) is a nervous worker assigned to Processor, newly on the job and eager to prove himself in a workplace full of hyper-efficient anacites. Hesop acts downtrodden and skittish when others browbeat or bully him, and at this point in his life he expects ridicule. He imagines his coworkers dislike him because he’s organic and therefore imagine his performance is inferior, when the truth is they’re curious about him and excited to have an organic colleague. Clearing up this misunderstanding or helping build Hesop’s confidence improves his attitude.

Adventure Role: Hesop acts as a liaison for the PCs’ investigation and can share information with them he’s not supposed to, like pointing them to a lead, pulling official documents or transcripts of queries to Insight Array, or giving them a clue they missed.

Making an Impression: Asking for his help, or simply being polite toward him, increases Hesop’s attitude to friendly. Taking actions to help him get along with his coworkers, such as counseling him, planning a team-building activity, or mediating a conversation and succeeding at a relevant DC 13 skill check increases his attitude to helpful. If the PCs routinely bully or belittle Hesop, he stops helping them and ignores their comms.

Ally Benefits: +1 circumstance bonus to one Computers or Thievery check per day (helpful).

Ghellon.name: Ghellon
Ghellon.text:
Ghellon

Ghellon (charming jaded female android entrepreneur) owns Analog Cafe, a famous establishment in downtown Striving. Originally from the Nitilema slums on Verces, Ghellon doesn’t remember all her personas—companion, hacker, porter, thug—before she bought a shuttle pass to Aballon and rebooted her life. She used dirty money to acquire Analog and tipped the algorithm, local slang for bribing an official to rig your Insight Array assignment, allowing her to create a small hospitality empire. Twenty-three years of excellent service, safe spectacle, and culture have earned Ghellon a position of respect in the community.

A newly honest businessperson, Ghellon enjoys bartending and working the floor alongside her robotic staff. She handles most difficult customer service situations.

Adventure Role: Ghellon might guide the PCs if their investigation stalls, feed them info they missed framed as juicy gossip she overheard, or just pour them free drinks and commiserate while they discuss where to go next. If her attitude is helpful, Ghellon might help bail the PCs out of a tight spot, such as by showing up to defend them in a trial.

Making an Impression: Ghellon’s weakness is flattery (@Check[diplomacy|dc:14|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression]) or deception (@Check[deception|dc:14|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Make an Impression]), though she tersely denies it. She likes big tippers (20 credits or more) and anyone who can mix her favorite cocktail, a Cuvacara @Check[beverage-lore|dc:14|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Sunset], @Check[chemistry-lore|dc:14|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Sunset], or @Check[society|dc:14|traits:action:make-an-impression|name:Sunset] (the drink has notes of diesel, sweat, and orange juice). Once per week, a success at any of these checks increases her attitude by one step; critical failure decreases her attitude by one step unless she’s already helpful toward someone in the party.

Ally Benefits: +1 circumstance bonus to one Diplomacy, Deception, or Intimidation check per week (friendly); free drinks (helpful).

NPC Gallery.name: NPC Gallery
NPC Gallery.text:
NPC Gallery

The player characters meet many interesting nonplayer characters (NPCs) over the course of their adventure. They’ll surely befriend some—and perhaps make life-long enemies of others! The following NPCs play an important role in the adventure; the PCs might spend more time with some, or want to learn more about others. Feel free to develop deeper story roles for any NPCs you like, and use those presented here as samples to develop guidelines for Making an Impression and earning Ally Benefits from other NPCs as needed.

Government.name: Government
Government.text:
Government

Laws might seem redundant for residents who can program themselves to cooperate, but rules help organic cultures peacefully intermix with machine protocols. Insight Array is Aballon’s governing body. They are a conglomerate of anacites making decisions based on complex algorithms and intelligent databases.

Insight Array (sometimes called IA) connects Aballon’s residents through a virtual app that anyone can download onto a comm unit or other computer for free (or connect directly via shortwave network in the case of constructs). Downloading the Insight Array app helps characters stay connected and access everything from emergency alerts to public transportation and paying side jobs. The app monitors all visitors and residents to ensure they have appropriate lodging, comfortable conditions, and healthy sustenance, plus a small luxury stipend of UPBs in exchange for completing work determined by a complex set of algorithms.

A judicial authority commonly called the Machine Court rules on everything from planetary laws to personal disputes. The council of robotic judges offers unbiased trials for androids and other constructs, and machines flock to Aballon from across the Pact Worlds and further corners of space seeking the Machine Court’s ruling.

Striving.name: Striving
Striving.text:
Striving

Life in Striving

“Downgrid” generally means south of Central Circuit, which is located exactly in the middle of the city. Likewise, “upgrid” is another popular term referring to the region north of this landmark. Blocks are usually called “circuits,” a trend popularized by organic residents as more of them moved to the metal city.

Striving’s weather and the day/night cycle are unique, and often catch visitors and new residents by surprise. “Fullbright” indicates midday, the period from cycle 4 to 6 when the sun shines brightest; most organics avoid the outdoors during this time, remaining in the shade of orbital plates, roofed buildings, and underground complexes.

Every day at dawn and dusk, gas billows up from the streets as the atmosphere generators kick off their cycle. If it was a particularly hot day, or a temperature shift is occurring, the clouds condense into gentle rain that makes the city shine like glass.

A glistening metal slab shears through smooth gray rock, stacked with delicate structures and tiered solar panels that sway in the upper atmosphere like wind chimes. Swirling domes of gases churn around dense clusters of metal and industry, dotting the industrial gray landscape that is the prime megaplex, an immense metropolis where intelligent machines and organic creatures are forever working together toward the goal of utopia.

Striving has metastasized into a rambling city of tidy grids that stretches for hundreds of miles across Aballon’s surface. It’s the prime megaplex on the planet and is home to most of the world’s industry and most of its inhabitants. The city’s layout is simple, but its scale is so large and its architecture so intricate that most visitors get lost in the place they call “Metal City” without a guide or the handy Insight Array app.

Center Circuit forms Striving’s core, surrounded by orderly districts dedicated to industry, recharging and residential facilities, commerce, and entertainment. Striving is a forest of towering skyscrapers and platforms with roots reaching miles below the ground. A few vast orbital plates glide through this metal landscape like massive barges, carrying mechanical foundries, entertainment complexes, and security outposts. High-speed trains and a robust multi-level highway system connect the city’s far-flung locations, making treks across the megaplex in minutes. A defensive perimeter known as Firewall protects the city from the harsh environment and aggressive wildlife outside.

Environment and Weather.name: Environment and Weather
Environment and Weather.text:
Environment and Weather

Outside the lower atmosphere, at about 1,800 feet, the air is incredibly thin. Creatures who aren’t acclimated must attempt a Fortitude save each hour they breathe thin air, or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} (and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} on a critical failure). The effect persists until the creature gets 8 hours of rest. Acclimating means a creature has spent at least 1 week living in the environment with daily exposure.

During daylight hours, the sun is incredibly harsh outside the protective atmosphere, and temperatures can spike up to 139 degrees F. Creatures are exposed to this heat when venturing outside a city or stepping outside the elevator in a charging platform, immediately feeling the scorching sun beating down on them. Creatures must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:12] save every 10 minutes or take @Damage[1d4[fire]] damage. Most creatures can’t survive Aballon’s heat without environmental protections.

At night, temperatures plunge to –20 degrees F (@Damage[1d4[cold]] damage every 10 minutes) for 6 hours. This period, known as Fulldark, is widely considered one of the most dangerous times to be outside the safety of climate-controlled megaplexes.

Wandering in rural Aballon is dangerous but not necessarily fatal. Lost travelers claim to have been saved by a roaming barathu explorer who treks the wilderness like a living supply barge laden with gas reserves, spare thermal gear, and unbelievably delicious victuals.

Culture.name: Culture
Culture.text:
Culture

Striving’s culture is eclectic and mercurial. High-speed travel and infospheres connect a metropolis inhabited by a diverse population of anacites, androids, SROs, humans, kasathas, ysoki, skittermanders, vesk, and any other species commonly found in the Pact Worlds (and a few rarely seen outside their distant part of the galaxy) who have built thriving communities. Ideas and trends spread fast, but Striving’s residents tend to value work and community. Most are environmentally conscious, making an effort to reduce and recycle waste, and keep a live-and-let-live-attitude toward their neighbors.

Anacites toil ceaselessly and tend their own affairs but are generally welcoming to newcomers. Anacite architects carefully design buildings with organic creatures as well as machines in mind. Most buildings have retractable roofing for solar power, while sensitive machinery and organic residences and workplaces are safely shielded from the sun and elements, usually located on lower floors or in insulated underground bunkers. Off-worlders can easily acquire environmental protection upgrades in the form of a quick-applying nanite spritz available in vending machines at any major port or transportation hub.

As Striving’s organic populations grow, Insight Array frequently assigns organic visitors to important tasks, realizing that their knowledge is equally important and their abilities are increasingly useful in this changing world.

Aballon.name: Aballon
Aballon.text:
Aballon

Aballon

Atmosphere: Thin

Gravity: Normal

Climate: Extreme; terraforming is common in megaplexes

Terrain: Terrestrial, rocky, isolated frozen rainforest (Ice Wells)

Population: Dense (megaplexes), sparse or deserted (outside firewalls)

Aballon is a rugged world near the Pact System’s sun inhabited by intelligent machines that have adapted to thrive within its harsh conditions. Some tourists might carelessly mislabel this planet a cold network of metastasizing metal cities run by industrious robots, but a tragic mystery lies at the core of this world. The lost prehistoric culture widely called the First Ones created living, thinking machines to build an outpost on Aballon, then abandoned them. Anacites—the machines’ name for themselves—continue laboring and upgrading themselves in their creators’ absence, endlessly debating whether their creators should decide their ultimate purpose and future as a species, or if they should become something new.

Visitor Center.name: Visitor Center
Visitor Center.text:
Visitor Center

What began as a drab corner of Striving set aside for the comfort and safety of organic beings has become a lively neighborhood of open-air markets and airy condos alive with neon lights and a wild mixture of smells and sounds at all times of the cycle. Vendor stalls line the pipes and corridors around squat, piecemeal metal buildings, most of which are split between shops and residences. Visitor Center is crowded and lively, but a few lucky residents have scored prime pads in the lofty rooftops, whether through genuine luck of the algorithm or monetary manipulation of the system.

The people who live in Visitor Center are mostly organic lifeforms or androids and SROs who moved here from other home worlds. The architecture and amenities of Visitor Center are all designed for organic lifeforms, with a focus on shelter from the sun and comfortable facilities to take care of biological needs like eating and sleeping. Most of the hotels and rentable accommodations that are suitable for organic creatures can be found in Visitor Center.

Outside shops, metal walls are covered with layers of posters and advertisements featuring organic models. Maintenance drones sporadically sweep the section and clean trash or perform maintenance checks, but otherwise relatively few synthetic people are typically seen walking the streets here.

Massive holoprojectors are crammed onto nearly every building and street corner in Visitor Center, mostly advertising shop wares, local entertainment, and the free Insight Array app. It can take some time for visitors to become accustomed to the constant barrage of visual and auditory stimulation, though most anacites can tune out whatever they deem irrelevant to their current task. Occasionally, holos flash emergency alerts, such as security warnings or weather advisories. Tiny vendor stalls sell food or nanopress, thin pliable sheets of soft metal used for printing scientific essays, fashion magazines, philosophical treatises, catalogs, and whatever else a publisher desires.

Unification Cathedral.name: Unification Cathedral
Unification Cathedral.text:
Unification Cathedral

The trinary structures of the Unification Cathedral rise above the megaplex, representing the three aspects of Triune. Below the triple-domed cathedral is a vast undercity called Ascension, where Drift beacons and engines are forged by Triunite clergy. Sacred legends say that Epoch’s neural network runs throughout Ascension, which was so named for the god’s artificial creation. Outside the cathedral’s perfect metal walls, fearsome Trifold Legionaries—elite technological holy warriors—stand guard protecting the secrets of their faith.

Transparency.name: Transparency
Transparency.text:
Transparency

Described as a glass mountain reflecting the cogs of a great machine, this monolith serves as the headquarters of the Striving Machine Court. Tiered courtrooms ascend inside the building, each the seat of an esteemed machine judge qualified to decide cases on behalf of the body of 37 judges with good standing in the organization. A host of bureaucrats cater to the judge’s every whim and make sure trials run smoothly; some unscrupulous officials abuse their power to nudge justice in their favor.

Theology Channel.name: Theology Channel
Theology Channel.text:
Theology Channel

Theology channel spirals out from the massive holy cathedral in rings. A path of precisely cut smooth stone and metal tiles, some slate gray and others striated with crystal, cuts through tiers of smaller structures. Many of these buildings look like squat metal shipping containers perched on ridges and adorned with prayer banners and garlands indicating the gods worshipped there. Others are structures built painstakingly to resemble traditional architecture found on other worlds. Rumor has it the architect chose this design to symbolize the tenets of Singularitism as applied to the gods.

Striving for Divinity

Striving is considered the holy city of @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.deities.Item.OSQPUVZrtxJUisPa]{Triune} because of the presence of Epoch’s neural network. Long ago, machines sought to create their own god and constructed a vast supercomputer beneath the city. Their ardent belief and industry spawned Epoch, who would later join with Brigh and Casandalee to become Triune.

Many Triunites believe this merging was only the beginning. Priests of Triune welcomed other faiths to their holy city and helped them establish shrines and temples to their gods. They believe that by learning about others’ faiths, mortals might reach an accord that will allow their gods to join Triune and create the Singularity—a new divinity that every being, god and mortal, will be part of.

Occasionally, the fabric of reality around Striving is disturbed as Epoch’s synapses fire. Something—perhaps the artificial god—protected Striving from @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.deities.Item.frkwaiKRQnE8s5QQ]{The Newborn's} psychic scream. Most people who live in Striving feel shielded by the city’s spirits.

Polytechnica.name: Polytechnica
Polytechnica.text:
Polytechnica

While the Unification Cathedral explores divinity, Polytechnica seeks to solve everything else. Dedicated to unraveling mysteries of history, mathematics, and science, Polytechnica is an institution of learning and research headquartered in a campus near downgrid Striving, with hundreds of smaller annexes scattered across the megaplex. Polytechnica’s buildings are all constructed of minerals harvested from the planet in a unique, brutalist architectural style favored by anacite builders. Polytechnica’s annexes have vastly different forms and functions, including glass-paneled greenhouses of flora, supercooled server rooms, and high-tech hospitals.

Polytechnica’s arcane and occult magic wings are some of the most diverse in the institution. Anacite adepts practice technomancy and prototype new hybrid arts. Many of the most delicate magical archives are run by sages who follow @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.deities.Item.YiV6Wd2OxCOxy00A]{Yaraesa's} path by curating and protecting ancient data repositories.

The Prime Archive is a sacred shrine as much as it’s a repository and library dedicated to the First Ones. The Prime Archive is full of relics taken from sites all over the Pact Worlds, many of which are still unidentified.

Downtime: Lectures and workshops about a wide variety of topics are hosted everywhere around Polytechnica’s sprawling campus. Players who created their own custom characters for this adventure (or who want to customize their premade characters now that they’ve had a chance to play) can retrain in half the normal time if they attend lectures during downtime. A PC who attends 10 classes on the same topic becomes trained in one Lore skill or language of their choice. Attending one class requires spending 4 hours of downtime.

Magenta.name: Magenta
Magenta.text:
Magenta

This semi-legal gambling parlor is always on the move, staying a few steps ahead of the authorities who largely ignore the lucrative operation that keeps tourism pouring into Striving. Magenta is a casino depot built atop a hovering orbital plate about 500 feet wide. Inside, the plush decor mimics a fairytale castle with a pink-and-purple color palette. Staff (mostly organic) dress in costume as royalty and serve customers with posh accents. In the dozens of gambling halls, games of all types from everywhere in the galaxy can be played. Drinks are on the house as long as you’re playing.

Firewall.name: Firewall
Firewall.text:
Firewall

Firewall is a defensive perimeter of guard posts, some stationary and others affixed to mobile platforms that float slowly 5 to 30 feet above the ground. Protector bots, wingbots, and other anacites designed for surveillance and protection are stationed at each post. They spend their time monitoring zones for any unusual activity, including dangerous wildlife, hazardous weather, or raiding parties of alien invaders or armed scavengers. Such threats are relatively rare because of how efficiently Firewall’s patrollers perform their jobs. By nature, the anacites stationed along the Firewall are protective of anyone they assess to be less capable in self-defense, but they’re welcoming to those who can prove themselves.

Central Circuit.name: Central Circuit
Central Circuit.text:
Central Circuit

This district is set up like a circuit board, with individual “components” or work sites connected by tubes and tunnels inside a massive metal complex that spans the entirety of the miles-wide district. Many corridors are configurable, allowing them to function as switches and regulate the flow of traffic through the complex much as a circuit’s switches conduct power. Thousands of anacites and a handful of other life-forms are assigned to work in Central Circuit, mostly performing administrative tasks, data analysis, and surveillance or logistical work.

Analog.name: Analog
Analog.text:
Analog

This famed cafe is one of Striving’s favorite spots. Beloved for the atmosphere and the delicious food, everybody from politicians to wealthy businesspeople to renowned scientists has dined here. Nobody knows why the cafe’s owner gave it this ironic name, but it’s certainly memorable, and the rumored owner and bartender @UUID[JournalEntry.sf2av00504npcgal.JournalEntryPage.04ghellon0000000]{Ghellon} isn’t telling.

Hot spots.name: Hot spots
Hot spots.text:
Hot spots

Striving is an immense megaplex with millions of residents and an unimaginable number of interesting locales to visit; the locations detailed here are some of those that feature prominently in the Murder in Metal City adventure, but GMs could use these as inspiration to invent any number of other locations to suit their needs.

Terrain.name: Terrain
Terrain.text:
Terrain

In megaplexes like Striving, the terrain is urban, made of treated metal and rock with airlock doors and high-tech security. Difficult terrain due to crowds and cover due to both tight spaces and unusual architecture are common. The rocky terrain outside the megaplexes varies between barren, exposed plains and steep, craggy ridges. Inside Ice Wells, terrain is icy; slipping is a concern when attempting to Balance or Climb.

Climate and Weather.name: Climate and Weather
Climate and Weather.text:
Climate and Weather

Like every other Aballonian megaplex, a thick dome of gases envelops Striving, supplying breathable air to the many organic residents and protecting them from the planet’s brutal day/night cycle.

Inside Striving’s dome, temperatures never rise above 73 degrees F and never dip below 60—until last year. Lately, heat waves have spiked temperatures to a balmy 80 degrees F, made worse by air pumps increasing humidity. The heat waves have been happening more frequently, and Insight Array isn’t sure why.

Because of the pumps that generate localized atmosphere for Striving, residents of the megaplex sometimes experience unique “weather” phenomena. Every evening the megaplex’s condensers vent, creating thick fog and sometimes a cool, gentle “rain” inside Striving’s atmospheric bubble.

Current Events.name: Current Events
Current Events.text:
Current Events

Striving is usually a tranquil place. Residents are placid and prefer to coexist or settle their disagreements through calm and rational debate rather than violent confrontation.

The Wreck of the Returned has increased local interest in First Ones sites. Striving Polytechnica was chosen to study some relics, but has lost several, leading to controversy and unwanted attention for the institute. There are already whispers that they’re being cased by an undercover Stewards operation.

Many locals remember an infamous minor controversy in 309 AG when a large number of non-anacites were assigned tasks by the Insight Array. An anacite bureaucrat and Machine Court judge challenged the assignments, which included engineering in Central Circuit and security at Striving’s Firewall. The rogue judge was ultimately overruled, but the court’s reputation was already tarnished.

Artificial Beings.name: Artificial Beings
Artificial Beings.text:
Artificial Beings

Many types of artificial beings live in Striving, from the near-omnipresent Insight Array to individual anacite units and automated robots.

The term Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Starfinder is used for artificial personalities that gain full sapience, or attract a soul. Androids, anacites, SROs, and living holograms are all versions of artificial intelligences. Legend has it that sometimes a virtual intelligence can awaken through experience, magic, or some spiritual means and become a true AI.
